READY ARMOR
Architecture · Capability · Evidence
READY ARMOR / REFALL CONTROL · CAPABILITY · EVIDENCE

REFALL AB

Persistent research loops. Bounded work. Reviewable evidence.

REFALL AB makes a research campaign persistent across worker conversations and manager sessions. Shared coverage, evidence, obligations, scoped launch decisions, and checked closeout connect bounded work to reviewable conclusions.

01 / IN PRACTICE

Use cases and outcomes.

Source security research

Combine measured source examination with attack-surface review, candidate findings, verification, and remediation work.

A reviewable evidence trail, explicit unresolved work, and findings linked to source and reproduction material.

Reverse engineering and architecture mapping

Accumulate component determinations, interface observations, flow relationships, saved analysis, and a technical narrative.

A persistent codex that later workers can extend without repeating the entire examination.

Compiled-binary investigations

Use the standalone binary family to seed function questions, examine decompilation, challenge claims, and collect runtime proof.

Function-anchored research, explicit validation blockers, and reproducible finding packages when proof is available.

Long research campaigns

Coordinate bounded specialist work across interrupted execution, provider changes, unresolved decisions, and repeated report revisions.

Resumable subject state with archived evidence, current analyst notes, and an inspectable closeout decision.
READY ARMOR / CONTROL IN DEPTH

Build control from the boundary up.

REFALL controls campaign resources, brokered launch decisions, scheduled work, and evidence acceptance. Runtime mounts and tool permissions supply the execution boundary. Recorded receipts keep scope decisions and completion reviewable.

Lowest implemented boundary first. Select a layer to inspect its checks, activation, and decision scope.

LAYER 01operation gate

Source and workspace projection

Boundary
Host source directory to the configured Agent Canvas container.
Implemented mechanism
Resolve the source directory, validate the subject name, inspect the container, and reuse its matching mount or copy source files.
Decision or effect
Invalid source directories, unsafe subject names, and failed projection cannot complete this synchronization route.
Activation and coverage
Backend launch supplies an available source path. Existing Docker mounts retain their configured access mode.

Code-path example

INPUT

Project a missing source directory or an unsafe subject name.

RESULT

Synchronization raises AgentWorkspaceError. A copied directory remains an ordinary container directory.

LAYER 02observation

Content identity and source observations

Boundary
Configured source root to the campaign inventory.
Implemented mechanism
Hash file content and record relative paths, file facts, unreadable files, and symlink observations.
Decision or effect
No worker operation is blocked by inventory collection. Membership supports later finding checks.
Activation and coverage
Inventory enumeration runs for source intake or an explicit inventory refresh.

Code-path example

INPUT

A file symlink resolves outside the source root.

RESULT

Record an off-root observation. File facts can still read the resolved file.

↗ build_source_inventory L66↗ _symlink_observation L179
LAYER 03operator authority

Authenticated capability changes

Boundary
Capability grant and revoke HTTP routes.
Implemented mechanism
Compare X-REFALL-Operator-Token with the configured token file. Replace the supplied grantor with operator after authentication.
Decision or effect
Unauthenticated grant or revoke requests are refused when token protection is configured.
Activation and coverage
Set REFALL_CAPABILITY_OPERATOR_TOKEN_PATH to a readable token file. The default unset value disables token authentication and retains caller-supplied grantor identity.

Code-path example

INPUT

Submit a grant without the configured operator token.

RESULT

HTTP 403; no grant is stored. An unreadable credential file gives HTTP 503.

↗ require_capability_operator L23–33↗ grant_capability L101
LAYER 04policy gate

Scoped authorization decisions

Boundary
An action request presented to the capability broker.
Implemented mechanism
Require a class and declared effects. Match an active grant against applicable target and effect conditions.
Decision or effect
Requests with no matching unexpired grant receive a refusal decision.
Activation and coverage
Call /execution/authorize or use a backend caller that consults the store. Scope checks depend on populated request and grant fields.

Code-path example

INPUT

Request a host, method, or path outside the configured grant.

RESULT

Return accepted:false with refusal reasons and record the API decision. This decision-only route launches no command; callers must obey refusal.

↗ CoverageStore.authorize_execution L1458↗ _grant_refusal_reasons L1785–1806↗ authorize_execution L171
LAYER 05operation gate

Backend process release

Boundary
Named Start or Update command to the standing-loop process.
Implemented mechanism
Apply operation switches and the command allowlist. Authorize the subject-path run_local_command request before launch.
Decision or effect
A refused capability decision prevents this backend route from starting the loop process.
Activation and coverage
Enable REFALL_ENABLE_OPS and REFALL_ENABLE_OPS_COMMANDS; both default false. Loop launch defaults true. Disabled launch skips authorization and starts no process.

Code-path example

INPUT

Start a subject without a matching process grant.

RESULT

HTTP 403 before process launch. Start without stored context returns HTTP 409.

↗ require_ops_commands L115↗ run_command L123↗ _start_subject L266↗ _authorize_process_launch L386–403
LAYER 06task gate

Work selection and claim allocation

Boundary
Stored work to a scheduled subject, unit, or finding assignment.
Implemented mechanism
Prioritize obligations, subject setup, fresh breadth, finding work, and later unit passes. Use claims and per-target progress.
Decision or effect
Eligible selection branches skip modules with unmet dependencies, completed target work, duplicate active target work, matching exclusions, or exhausted module slots.
Activation and coverage
Standing-loop selection applies branch-specific conditions. Fresh breadth bypasses module eligibility; later unit selection omits unit_state. Global concurrency still applies.

Code-path example

INPUT

A later unit pass does not match its path filter or has an unmet dependency.

RESULT

Skip that pass. Fresh characterization uses direct coverage claims and the global conversation limit.

↗ RefallStandingLoop._claim_next_task L590↗ eligible_modules L333↗ ModuleScheduler.next_unit_module L472
LAYER 07task gate

Conversation and recovery bounds

Boundary
A scheduled assignment to the Agent Canvas conversation API.
Implemented mechanism
Send the task workspace, provider settings, objective, and max_iterations. Classify failures before bounded retry.
Decision or effect
Recognized scope, capability, and operator-stop outcomes do not receive ordinary automatic worker retries.
Activation and coverage
The normal dispatcher sends conversation limits to Agent Canvas. Fresh characterization requests 30 iterations; recoverable worker retries default to two attempts.

Code-path example

INPUT

A worker reports scope_blocked or capability_missing.

RESULT

Preserve available output and create an operator or capability obligation instead of repeating the action.

↗ AgentCanvasDispatcher.start L205↗ OHClient.start_conversation L89↗ classify_invocation L23
LAYER 08model guidance

Scope and workspace instructions

Boundary
Campaign context to specialist reasoning and tool choice.
Implemented mechanism
Build an objective from stored context, scope, target, module, routing, output requirements, source location, and scratch location.
Decision or effect
These instructions request in-scope behavior. They do not mechanically prevent external tool actions.
Activation and coverage
The dispatcher constructs the specialist initial message.

Code-path example

INPUT

RESULT

The worker receives explicit writing instructions. Actual write permissions come from mounts and process access.

LAYER 09task gate

Continuation input comparison

Boundary
A checkpointed campaign to a resumed standing loop.
Implemented mechanism
Compare recorded input hashes with current source and configuration hashes through resume preflight.
Decision or effect
A returned drift refusal stops the supported resume path and exposes a decision obligation.
Activation and coverage
Prior checkpoints and the preflight API are available. Missing optional support and some service errors bypass refusal.

Code-path example

INPUT

RESULT

Record resume_preflight_refused and stop that continuation path.

LAYER 10observation

Continuous result capture

Boundary
Worker events and workspace results to persistent campaign evidence.
Implemented mechanism
Read conversation events and submission files during execution. Terminal handling classifies, parses, checks identity, and preserves observations before handling the classified outcome.
Decision or effect
Observation itself does not stop the worker action that produced a result.
Activation and coverage
Standing-loop polling and completion run ingestion. Structured terminal submission remains optional unless REFALL_REQUIRE_STRUCTURED_SUBMIT is enabled.

Code-path example

INPUT

A worker fails after it produced useful facts or artifacts.

RESULT

Preserve available output, classify the failure, and expose repair or operator work.

↗ RefallStandingLoop._incremental_ingest L1115↗ RefallStandingLoop._finish_conversation L1378↗ RefallStandingLoop._block_empty_subject_module_completion L1161
LAYER 11record gate

Finding admission and declared scope

Boundary
A proposed finding to canonical finding storage.
Implemented mechanism
Require evidence, confidence, and source or artifact references. Check available inventory membership and explicit external-target scope.
Decision or effect
Unsupported or out-of-scope candidates are refused admission to the finding store.
Activation and coverage
add_finding evaluates a proposed record after worker activity. Inventory membership is advisory when inventory is unavailable; external URL hosts require explicit scope.

Code-path example

INPUT

A candidate cites https://outside.example.test without that host in explicit external_targets.

RESULT

Refuse promotion. The API records the refusal and creates review work.

↗ evaluate_finding_candidate L12↗ CoverageStore.add_finding L749
LAYER 12record gate

Typed finding transitions

Boundary
Existing finding state to a new status or quality tier.
Implemented mechanism
Check current status, allowed states, receipt types, evidence references, pending contradictions, and supplied source hashes.
Decision or effect
A refused transition preserves the existing finding state and records the refused attempt.
Activation and coverage
The transition path receives a proposed decision. Hash freshness checks activate when the receipt supplies source or configuration hashes.

Code-path example

INPUT

Mark a finding FALSE_POSITIVE without an accepted receipt type and evidence.

RESULT

Refuse the transition. Live validation, duplicate, downgrade, and chain deferral have separate receipt requirements.

↗ CoverageStore.transition_finding L1008↗ _receipt_stale_reasons L112↗ CoverageStore.update_finding_validation L974
LAYER 13record gate

Persistent resolution obligations

Boundary
Open or claimed pending work to a terminal resolution.
Implemented mechanism
Keep missing access, blocked scope, incomplete evidence, and refused decisions in pending records. Validate required resolution receipts.
Decision or effect
Required receipt failures prevent pending-action resolution; open obligations can block closeout.
Activation and coverage
Resolve, defer, or cancel a pending action. Required types vary by action; an untyped done action does not universally require evidence.

Code-path example

INPUT

Defer an obligation without evidence references.

RESULT

Reject the resolution. Required receipt types must match and include evidence.

↗ CoverageStore.finish_pending_action L1243↗ CoverageStore.trigger_pending_actions_for_runtime_event L1346
LAYER 14record gate

Report replacement protection

Boundary
Enriched report content to the current report object.
Implemented mechanism
Compare populated report sections before replacing the current formal report. Retain a refused candidate as a diagnostic object.
Decision or effect
An unapproved structural downgrade cannot replace the current report through this assembly path.
Activation and coverage
assemble_report defaults allow_structural_downgrade to false. Explicit override bypasses this guard. Generic object writes use a separate API path.

Code-path example

INPUT

Replace a rich report with a candidate that loses protected sections.

RESULT

Return downgrade_refused and keep the current report.

↗ assemble_report L16
LAYER 15record gate

Campaign closeout acceptance

Boundary
Current campaign records to a closed lifecycle result.
Implemented mechanism
Check pending actions, receipts, refused transitions, finding proof, expired claims, context, and report freshness.
Decision or effect
Blocking failures prevent a successful closed result from the closeout operation.
Activation and coverage
Named Closeout or the loop manager evaluates the gate. Draft/current reports can already exist; this gate controls the closed lifecycle result.

Code-path example

INPUT

Close a campaign with open pending work or a stale report.

RESULT

Return blocked and record loop.closeout.blocked. Coverage below 95 percent is advisory.

↗ evaluate_closeout_gate L14↗ _closeout_subject L570↗ RefallLoopManager.closeout L81
LAYER 16operator authority

Recorded closeout exceptions

Boundary
A declared operator exception to selected closeout checks.
Implemented mechanism
Require check IDs and a nonempty receipt. Append an accepted override entry and make matching failed checks nonblocking warnings.
Decision or effect
Missing check IDs or receipt prevent this override route from accepting the exception.
Activation and coverage
The override route receives an explicit decision record. It records the supplied operator name without capability-token authentication; deployment access control establishes caller authority.

Code-path example

INPUT

Accept a selected closeout exception with a receipt and reason.

RESULT

Keep the failed condition visible as an overridden warning and retain the ledger reference.

↗ override_closeout_gate L33↗ _apply_override L421

04 / END-TO-END TRACES

A complete path through the system.

Follow each operation from its entry point through decisions, state changes, evidence, and review.

The campaign cycle

One coordinator pass selects work, polls conversations, retains evidence, refreshes records, and saves continuation state. A dashed return represents another eligible coordinator cycle.

  1. 01

    Select recorded work

    Claim worker-eligible pending actions first. Then consider threat-model or subject setup, fresh coverage, finding work, and later unit modules.

    ↗ _claim_next_task L590–636
  2. 02

    Dispatch bounded work

    Prepare the task workspace and provider lane. Send the task objective with its conversation iteration limit.

    ↗ start L205
  3. 03

    Poll active conversations

    Read active worker status. Ingest available events and structured files while a conversation remains active.

    ↗ run L442↗ _incremental_ingest L1115
  4. 04

    Retain evidence and decide

    Classify terminal results, parse output, check submission identity, and retain useful observations before outcome handling. Completion and retry use their own checks.

    ↗ _finish_conversation L1378
  5. 05

    Refresh shared records

    Update determinations and applicable report state. Report and visualization workers have their own cadence and slot rules.

    ↗ _maybe_write_determinations L1711↗ _maybe_refresh_report L1769↗ _maybe_dispatch_report_agent L1804
  6. 06

    Save and continue or return

    Persist active conversations and coordinator state. Module completion has a separate progress store. Continue when configured and eligible; idle, stalls, or limits can return control.

    ↗ _write_state L2163↗ run L442↗ _save_module_progress L429–440

Passes on one target

Example security-pack path. Unit dependencies are local to that unit. Finding verification targets finding records; review does not have to produce a finding.

  1. 01

    Characterize a unit

    Default security assessment pulls in characterization through its dependencies. Explicit baseline selection supports characterization-only work.

    ↗ PACKS.security_assessment L142–157↗ ModuleRegistry L211↗ _task_for_characterize L653↗ ModuleRegistry executable default L235–249
  2. 02

    Map its attack surface

    The security reconnaissance module follows characterization on the same target. Identify inputs, parsers, privileges, and trust boundaries.

    ↗ PACKS.security_assessment L142–157↗ _task_for_unit_module L676↗ next_unit_module L472
  3. 03

    Review concrete risks

    The security review module follows reconnaissance for that unit. Retain source evidence and candidate findings through the corresponding persistence paths.

    ↗ PACKS.security_assessment L142–157↗ next_unit_module L472↗ _persist_findings L2457
  4. 04

    Select finding verification

    When an eligible finding exists and finding work is selected, the security verification module receives that finding as its target.

    ↗ PACKS.security_assessment L142–157↗ next_finding_module L493↗ _task_for_finding_module L744
  5. 05

    Promotion and disposition use their own evidence and receipt checks. Accepted and refused decisions remain available to later work and closeout.

    ↗ transition_finding L1008

The resource feedback cycle

Tool delivery is a recorded resource workflow. Head cycles reread delivered items; compatibility research drivers load them at startup. The standing scheduler selects its own work queues.

  1. 01

    Record a resource need

    Create an open wishlist item with its kind, item, reason, and requester. Access and data needs can remain for operator handling.

    ↗ add_wishlist_item L1490–1512
  2. 02

    Check host availability

    The watchdog reads open and provided records. It skips matching provided tools and checks the host executable path for supported request kinds.

    ↗ _handle_wishlist L903–964
  3. 03

    Provide a supported tool

    An already available executable can be recorded as provided. When enabled, a fixed allowlisted installer can supply a missing tool; success must pass an executable check. Unhandled requests remain visible.

    ↗ _handle_wishlist L903–964↗ _install_wishlist_tool L995
  4. 04

    Record delivery and its receipt

    Append a new provided row and an ops-event ledger receipt linking the source request and delivery. The original request remains in history.

    ↗ _record_wishlist_provided L966–993↗ append_entry L41–57
  5. 05

    Brief later workers

    Each head cycle reads provided items. The research driver and three binary drivers include their startup snapshot in worker objectives, with instructions to avoid duplicate requests.

    ↗ run_cycle L40↗ format_provided_wishlist L4
  6. 06

    Continue authorized research

    Use resources in the appropriate host or worker environment. Resolve related obligations and obtain any required action grants through their separate APIs. A later need can create another wish.

    ↗ _claim_pending_action L1987↗ authorize_execution L1458

FIELD GUIDE / 0116 MIN READ

REFALL AB#

Persistent research loops for source code, binaries, and evidence.

REFALL AB coordinates specialist agents around a shared research workbench. It turns a subject into bounded work, records what each worker examined, and preserves the evidence behind each conclusion. A subject can continue across many conversations, interrupted workers, report revisions, and manager sessions.

The operator defines the objective and scope. The manager selects work and execution resources. Specialists inspect source, examine binaries, build harnesses, challenge claims, or compile reports. The workbench stores context, coverage, facts, leads, findings, artifacts, and outstanding decisions.

Why the design is distinctive#

A long investigation must retain more than its latest answer. It must preserve which material was examined, why a conclusion was accepted, and which questions remain open. REFALL makes those records part of the research system.

The subject owns the state. Workers receive bounded assignments, contribute observations, and return results through defined record paths. Later work can reuse the inventory, determinations, artifacts, finding history, and unresolved obligations after a conversation ends or a manager restarts.

The distinctive design connects four decisions:

DecisionMechanismWhy it matters
What should run next?Coverage claims, target-local module progress, and pending-action priority.Broad examination and focused follow-up share the same campaign.
What authority was granted?Scoped capability records and a backend launch caller that obeys broker refusal.An assignment and permission to perform an action remain separate decisions.
What conclusion is supported?Captured evidence, finding admission, and typed disposition receipts.A worker's narrative does not silently become an accepted finding state.
What counts as finished?Separate worker, module, report, and closeout conditions.Captured output, an idle loop, and campaign completion have different meanings.

These mechanisms reinforce each other through shared records. An interrupted worker can leave useful evidence without completing its assignment. A rejected or deferred finding can retain its proof and next obligation. A later worker or configured provider can extend that work without replacing the subject's history.

REFALL applies the Ready Armor approach at the campaign and evidence boundaries. Control in Depth separates the decisions; persistent records keep their results available to later workers and operators. These campaign controls run in backend services on the deployment host. Their enforcement comes from API admission, database transactions, authorization decisions, and checked record transitions. They do not require a virtual machine or container as their security foundation.

For example, backend Start and Update refuse an unauthorized launch before the new loop process starts. Finding admission and disposition routes also evaluate stored evidence and receipt requirements independently of the worker's prompt. The host supplies filesystem, network, and process permissions for tools that run directly. REFALL controls campaign decisions and evidence acceptance; direct specialist commands use the execution environment's permissions. Read Ready Armor in REFALL for the composition, practical value, and implementation paths.

What REFALL does#

A research campaign needs more than a sequence of agent replies. It needs a measured examination surface, clear ownership, reusable observations, and an explicit account of unfinished work. REFALL supplies those records and connects them to execution.

CapabilityResult for the operator
Subject workbenchesContext, evidence, decisions, and reports remain together for each target.
Evidence ledgerFacts, leads, findings, validation, artifacts, and operator decisions remain queryable after a worker ends.
Resource wishlistMissing tools or access become recorded requests, with provided records and delivery receipts.
Source inventoryFile identities and coverage units define the recorded examination surface.
Work modulesResearch, decomposition, review, harness creation, and verification can share one subject.
Specialist lanesReasoning, implementation, and verification work can use different providers.
Continuous evidence captureResults appear while workers run and survive incomplete conversations.
Finding gatesPromotion, rejection, duplicates, and deferral retain their supporting evidence.
Scoped capabilitiesGrants control requests presented to the broker; backend loop launch obeys its decision.
Persistent obligationsMissing access, failed output, and unanswered scope decisions remain visible.
Run continuityActive work, module progress, checkpoints, and shared notes survive a manager restart.
Evidence graphRecorded observation nodes and supplied relationship data form an inspectable evidence map.
Campaign supervisionLiveness checks, progress review, recovery limits, and configured usage ceilings support long campaigns.
Living reportsFindings, architecture, runtime proof, and analyst notes develop with the research.
Mechanical closeoutThe operator can inspect exactly which conditions prevent completion.

Research runs in connected cycles#

REFALL separates the campaign, the target-specific work, and each specialist conversation. A campaign can continue while individual workers finish, retry, or wait for a decision. The next assignment uses recorded state and the enabled module definitions.

The campaign cycle#

The standing loop fills available worker slots, polls active conversations, captures new evidence, updates reports, and saves run state. A polling cycle can collect partial output while a worker remains active. Worker completion has a separate outcome decision.

The scheduler selects the next task in this order:

  1. Claim an eligible pending action.
  2. Handle threat-model work and eligible subject-level setup modules.
  3. Claim a fresh coverage unit when breadth work is enabled.
  4. Select eligible finding work, such as verification or a patch proposal.
  5. Select later module work on previously examined units.

Dependencies apply to each target. A component can enter review while another component still needs its first examination. The default registry enables security assessment and adds its required characterization dependency. Select the baseline pack explicitly for characterization-only work.

The target-specific cycle#

The security assessment pack connects characterization, reconnaissance, and review for each coverage unit. Finding-specific verification uses the findings produced by the research.

Other packs add reverse engineering, general research, development, or toolchain work. A subject can combine packs and add custom modules with their own objectives and dependencies. The development pack includes a finding-scoped patch proposal. Patch verification requires the corresponding workflow configuration or assigned follow-up work.

Built-in modules run once per target. A custom module can set once_per_target: false to permit repeated eligible work. A pending action can request a focused investigation when a result needs more proof or an operator decision.

The worker and supervision cycles#

Each specialist receives a bounded task and an output contract. While it runs, REFALL can ingest facts, leads, findings, flows, and workspace artifacts. At termination, the executor retains useful evidence before it handles failure, retry, or successful completion. A failed conversation can contribute observations without completing its coverage unit.

The watchdog reviews services, progress, dependencies, and configured runtime, token, and cost limits. The supervisor combines frequent liveness checks with broader review and bounded recovery. A coordinator cycle limit controls polling work; active worker state can remain available for a later continuation. Repeated recovery can end in an operator hold.

Read Research cycles for the exact scheduling, retry, completion, and closeout paths. Open the interactive cycle maps to inspect the nodes and their source references.

The ledger is the campaign's research journal#

The subject ledger preserves evidence and decisions outside the current conversation. Entries can record facts, leads, findings, validation, artifacts, runtime events, capability decisions, pending actions, and closeout results. Each appended record receives an identifier and timestamps when those fields are absent.

The workbench stores the ledger as append-only JSONL. Queries can filter entries by kind, specialist lane, severity, and time. Statistics summarize the recorded kinds, lanes, and severities. This gives a replacement manager a durable account of what was examined, what changed, and why.

The Ops panel exposes a Ledger view and an Output view. Output compiles selected research records from the ledger. The report compiler also reads ledger entries and statistics alongside coverage and runtime state. A later report can therefore reuse earlier observations, validation, and artifact references.

Finding acceptance, coverage completion, and ledger capture have separate responsibilities. The finding gates validate accepted conclusions. Coverage tracks examined units and their determinations. The ledger retains the evidence and decision history behind those records.

Sources: ledger storage, ledger API, Ops panel.

The wishlist turns missing resources into visible requests#

A specialist can record a missing tool, dependency, access requirement, or other research need in the subject wishlist. The request carries its kind, item, reason, requester, and status. This preserves the need for the next operator or worker.

For supported tool requests, the watchdog checks whether the executable is already available on its host. When installation is enabled, it can run a fixed installer command for an allowlisted tool. The current installer table covers Binwalk, ExifTool, radare2, Rizin, and YARA, including the configured command aliases. Successful installation must also pass an executable availability check.

Delivery appends a separate provided wishlist row. An ops-event ledger entry links the original request, the provided record, and the delivery receipt. The original open request remains in history. The watchdog skips matching tools that already have a provided record.

The head orchestrator reads provided items for each head cycle. The research driver and three binary drivers load delivered items at startup and include that snapshot in their worker objectives. Their instructions tell workers to use delivered resources before requesting duplicates. Other resource needs remain available for operator handling. Host installation and worker-container availability are distinct deployment steps.

Wishes, obligations, and authority#

RecordWhat it controls
Wishlist itemA requested or provided research resource.
Pending actionAn unfinished obligation, with ownership, status, and any required resolution receipt.
Capability requestA request for permission to perform an action class.
Capability grantThe scope and conditions checked by the authorization broker.
Coverage claimA worker's lease on an examination unit.

The standing loop claims eligible pending actions before ordinary research work. An operator decision, fulfilled dependency, and authorized action each retain their own records. Use the corresponding resolution and grant paths to make blocked work eligible again.

Read Ledger and wishlist for request examples, API paths, delivery behavior, and the two dashboard interfaces.

Persistent memory connects the cycles#

REFALL maintains several records because each answers a different operational question.

RecordQuestion it answers
Subject context and scopeWhat are we examining, and under which boundaries?
Source inventory and coverageWhich exact files and units have been examined?
LedgerWhat evidence and decisions have accumulated?
BlackboardWhich compact shared notes should later tasks receive?
Module progressWhich passes have completed for each target?
WishlistWhich resources were requested or provided?
Pending actionsWhich obligations still need work or a decision?
Runtime observations and evidence graphWhich observations and supplied relationships were recorded?
Run manifest and checkpointsWhich providers, resources, inputs, and active work belong to this run?
Living report and analyst notesWhat does the accumulated research explain so far?

A manager restart can recover active conversations and module progress from stored state. Resume preflight compares recorded input hashes before it continues active work. Artifacts and archived conversations preserve details beyond a compact summary. The evidence graph exposes recorded nodes and supplied relationships. Call graphs and other code-analysis graphs remain separate tool outputs.

What the architecture combines#

Coverage and investigation serve different purposes. Coverage records which units were examined. Research follows concrete leads across callers, parsers, boundaries, and observed behavior. The two records let an operator distinguish broad examination from deeper proof.

Work belongs to the subject. The loop builds each task from stored context, scope, shared notes, its target, and an output contract. A replacement worker can read earlier determinations and artifacts before it extends the work. Expensive decompilation or source analysis can become reusable input for later passes.

Evidence collection continues during execution. REFALL reads agent-authored event messages and structured files in the worker workspace. It captures facts, leads, findings, and flow relationships while the conversation remains active. At termination, it also preserves useful results from interrupted or malformed output. Successful completion requires a separate decision.

Negative conclusions also require evidence. A finding cannot disappear through an unsupported false-positive or duplicate decision. Typed receipts record why the transition was accepted or refused. Source hashes can bind that proof to the files that were examined.

Publication has its own state. A current report has an explicit workbench object identifier. Report replacement checks preserve populated technical sections. Closeout examines unresolved obligations, proof, finding decisions, expired claims, and report freshness.

Who uses it#

AudienceTypical use
Security researchersTrace candidate vulnerabilities from source or binary anchors to review and runtime proof.
Reverse engineersBuild an accumulating map of components, interfaces, functions, and data flow.
Engineering reviewersCombine source examination, harness proposals, verification, and remediation work.
Research operatorsCoordinate long campaigns with bounded workers, reusable artifacts, and visible decisions.

For a firmware subject, the useful output can include a component inventory, function observations, validation requests, and a reproducible finding package. For a source repository, it can include per-file determinations, architecture facts, review results, and a prioritized research frontier. For a mapping task, facts, leads, and flow records can build a technical codex without vulnerability findings.

Ready Armor design approach#

The Ready Armor approach separates agent capability from operational authority. It also treats the provenance of a claim as a separate control concern. REFALL applies these ideas to research coordination: bounded assignments, recorded authority, durable evidence, explicit decisions, and reportable completion.

BRA provides a governed assessment architecture. ARA provides an agent runtime and policy substrate. REFALL provides a research campaign loop and evidence workbench. Their public architectures describe related control principles; REFALL's code supplies its own scheduler, result contracts, and decision gates. The control stack starts with configured source resources and execution permissions. Source projection prepares the container location; inventory records content identity. The broker then checks presented action requests against applicable grants. Backend Start and Update refuse process launch when that authorization fails.

Above execution, module selection bounds assignments and conversation requests carry iteration limits. Stored context guides the worker's scope and tool choices. Continuous capture preserves observations, while finding gates and typed receipts check accepted conclusions. Closeout checks whether unresolved work and report state permit a closed campaign result.

Each layer controls a different transition. The broker is a decision service, not a universal worker tool interceptor. Read-only source permissions come from configured mounts rather than the source-copy fallback. Grant authentication requires the configured operator token; an unset token leaves identity fields caller supplied. These boundaries let operators combine campaign controls with the execution environment's actual protections.

Read Ready Armor in REFALL for the design rationale and its distinctive research lifecycle. Read Control in depth for the layers, activation conditions, refusal sequence, and operator decisions. Read Research architecture for the wider responsibility model.

Source and binary research#

The main workbench flow runs the module scheduler through backend operations. It supports configurable subject, unit, and finding work. The repository also includes standalone source and binary research drivers. Those drivers use the compatibility coverage service and an investigation frontier.

Binary research starts from imported functions and their callers. Workers decompile selected functions, trace input, and enqueue concrete follow-up questions. Independent review challenges reachability and mitigations. Validation records reproduction attempts, observed effects, proof artifacts, and remaining blockers. Read Source and binary workflows for the execution families.

Start#

  1. Complete Installation.
  2. Configure the backend, Agent Canvas, and provider commands.
  3. Create a subject workbench.
  4. Generate and inspect its context.
  5. Select the work modules and execution scope.
  6. Start the loop through Operating procedures.
bash
python3 -m ref_all_executor subject create example --source-path /absolute/path/to/example
python3 -m ref_all_executor ops command context example
python3 -m ref_all_executor ops command doctor example
python3 -m ref_all_executor ops command estimate example
python3 -m ref_all_executor loop start example

The backend checks launch authorization before it starts the loop. The operator interface also exposes context, scope, threat model, coverage, pending actions, capabilities, runtime evidence, and closeout state.
