FIELD GUIDE / 0211 MIN READ

Ready Armor in REFALL AB#

REFALL applies the Ready Armor approach to sustained technical research. The campaign owns its state, evidence, and decisions. Worker conversations supply bounded examination and analysis.

The distinctive design connects work allocation, evidence capture, decision receipts, unresolved obligations, and the next research cycle. These mechanisms make earlier work usable after a conversation ends, a manager restarts, or another configured provider takes an assignment.

The research problem#

A long investigation contains several kinds of unfinished work. Some code remains unexamined. Some observations need interpretation. Some findings need reproduction. Some actions need authority or an execution resource. A report can be readable while these obligations remain open.

REFALL gives each condition a persistent record and a corresponding decision path. The next worker receives an assignment built from that shared state. The operator can inspect progress without treating the latest conversation as the entire campaign.

This design is useful when a subject needs repeated source examination, binary analysis, harness work, independent review, and report revisions. It also supports architecture mapping, where observations and relationships can be useful without vulnerability findings.

Capability, authority, observation, and acceptance#

Ready Armor separates useful capability from the authority to exercise it. It also separates an operation from the claim made about its result. REFALL expresses those distinctions through campaign records and checked transitions.

Control in Depth assigns each check to a defined operation or record transition. Persistent records keep the decision available to later workers and operators. Together, these principles connect immediate control with continuity across changes in the configured execution resources.

QuestionREFALL record or mechanismPractical effect
What can the worker contribute?Provider lane, task class, execution resources, and module objective.Assign reasoning, implementation, review, or reporting work deliberately.
Which work should run next?Claims, pending actions, module dependencies, and per-target progress.Coordinate fresh examination and later passes across workers.
Which presented action is authorized?Capability request, scoped grant, broker decision, and backend launch caller.Preserve the authority decision and enforce refusal on that launch path.
What was observed?Ledger entries, determinations, artifacts, and runtime observations.Retain material beyond the worker's final response.
What change is accepted?Finding admission, typed disposition receipts, and pending-action resolution.Check the record transition independently of the worker's narrative.
Is the campaign ready to close?Closeout checks over obligations, proof, claims, context, and report freshness.Make completion a visible decision about stored state.

The composition matters because each question can have a different answer. A permitted launch does not establish a validated finding. An examined unit does not establish that every behavior is safe. An idle coordinator does not establish campaign closeout.

Sources: scheduler, capability decisions, finding transitions, closeout.

Host deployment and concrete enforcement#

REFALL's campaign controls can operate as host services. A virtual machine or container is not the security foundation for these backend decisions. The enforcing code runs at API admission, work allocation, process release, record acceptance, and closeout. These checks evaluate requests and stored state independently of the worker's prompt content.

BoundaryEnforcing mechanismResult
Assignment ownershipA database transaction selects and leases an open or expired coverage unit.Concurrent claim requests receive coordinated ownership.
Enabled backend loop launchStart and Update call the capability broker before process creation.Broker refusal returns HTTP 403 before the new process starts.
Candidate findingAdmission checks evidence, confidence, references, available inventory, and explicit external-target scope.An unacceptable candidate receives refusal reasons.
Finding dispositionTyped receipts and applicable stored-state checks govern the requested transition.Narrative alone cannot perform the transition.
Campaign closeoutStored obligations, receipts, proof state, claims, context, and report freshness feed the closeout gate.Blocking conditions prevent an ordinary closed result.

The capability operator token protects grant and revoke routes when configured. It gives the backend an authenticated operator identity for those mutations. Without that setting, identity fields remain caller supplied. Protecting that API access is part of the deployment's authority boundary.

The same design separates campaign control from direct execution permissions. The host supplies filesystem, network, and process permissions. Agent Canvas and other execution resources apply their configured environment controls. A specialist's direct shell command does not automatically pass through REFALL's authorization broker. Brokered callers enforce its decision before they release their own supported action.

This division makes host deployment useful without assigning every security responsibility to one sandbox or one model instruction. The backend controls the campaign transitions it owns. The execution host controls the resources available to the running tools. The operator can inspect the retained authority decision, evidence, refusal, and next obligation.

Sources: claim transaction, launch authorization, operator authentication, finding admission, typed dispositions, closeout gate.

1. The subject retains the research#

A workbench groups context, source inventory, coverage, evidence, findings, obligations, and the current report pointer. These records have different lifecycles. Their separation lets the operator distinguish an observation, a hypothesis, an accepted conclusion, and a completion decision.

Source inventory identifies available content with paths, hashes, sizes, line counts, and file kinds. Coverage units turn part of that surface into claimable work. The ledger preserves appended evidence and decision records. Runtime storage retains events, observations, artifacts, manifests, and checkpoints.

A replacement manager can inspect those records before selecting further work. Later unit objectives explicitly ask workers to reuse prior summaries, findings, shared notes, and saved analysis. That guidance connects retained state with the next assignment. It does not depend on one model retaining an unlimited conversation history.

Sources: subject layout, inventory, ledger, reuse instructions.

2. Breadth and depth share one campaign#

Coverage establishes an examination surface. Module passes can then deepen the understanding of individual targets. The scheduler stores completed passes separately for each subject, unit, or finding target. A prerequisite completed on one unit does not satisfy another unit's prerequisite.

The standing loop prioritizes worker-claimable pending actions and subject setup before fresh breadth. Fresh coverage then precedes ordinary finding modules and later unit passes. The built-in security path connects characterization, reconnaissance, and review. Finding modules can request reproduction or a patch proposal.

This combination supports broad examination without losing focused questions. Pending actions provide a route for urgent validation. Local dependencies let different components advance at different rates. A custom module can add a concrete research objective without replacing the entire coordinator.

Claims coordinate ownership with leases. The backend selects open or expired units within a database transaction. Completed module identifiers persist separately from the current conversation. These controls reduce repeated allocation while keeping expired or unfinished work available for later examination.

Sources: coverage claims, module declarations, per-target progress.

3. Useful output survives an incomplete invocation#

A worker can produce useful analysis before it produces a final response. REFALL reads available conversation events and workspace results during execution. It can retain facts, leads, findings, flows, and saved analysis artifacts while the conversation remains active.

Terminal processing first classifies the invocation, parses its output, and checks submission identity. It then preserves available observations before handling the classified outcome or scheduling a replacement. A duplicate applied submission returns before terminal salvage.

Successful assignment completion has separate conditions. Characterization coverage submission requires its own completion branch. A module task without a unit record must produce durable canonical observations before its progress can advance. The campaign can therefore retain partial research while still showing an unfinished assignment.

This separation is useful when a provider stops, output is truncated, or a worker saves files without a complete final narrative. It preserves the available material for repair and review. It also keeps an execution failure from being reported as completed examination merely because some evidence was captured.

Sources: incremental ingestion, terminal order, empty-output check.

4. Conclusions have their own acceptance path#

The finding store checks proposed evidence, confidence, source references, and explicit external-target scope. Inventory membership is checked when inventory is available. A canonical finding can retain related evidence locations without representing each location as a different root cause.

Later finding decisions use typed receipts. False-positive, duplicate, downgrade, deferred-chain, and live-validation decisions have distinct requirements. Unresolved contradictory obligations can refuse a suppressive change. A receipt that supplies source hashes also activates applicable source-root and current-content checks.

These decisions preserve negative conclusions as well as positive findings. A later reviewer can inspect why a claim was rejected, deferred, reduced, or accepted. A supported research primitive can remain visible while its wider exploitability still needs examination.

The gates check specified record, reference, and receipt conditions. The operator reviews the interpretation and the meaning of the proof. A well-written explanation alone does not perform the corresponding finding transition.

Sources: candidate admission, canonical finding storage, disposition receipts.

5. Missing resources and missing authority remain distinct#

A wishlist records a requested tool, environment, access requirement, or other research resource. The watchdog can recognize host availability and process supported tool requests through its allowlisted installation path. Delivery appends a provided record and a linked ledger receipt. Supported head and research-driver prompts can include delivered resources in later objectives.

A pending action records work or a decision that remains unfinished. A capability grant records authority for a presented action class and scope. Providing a tool does not grant permission to use it against every target. Recording a capability request does not resolve the related obligation automatically.

Backend Start and Update provide a concrete release boundary. They consult the broker before an enabled loop process launch. A refused decision gives HTTP 403 before that process starts. Grant and revoke authentication requires the configured operator token file. Without that token setting, the API retains caller-supplied identities.

REFALL supplies those campaign and broker controls. The chosen execution environment supplies filesystem permissions, network boundaries, and any direct tool interception. The generic authorization endpoint records a decision without executing an arbitrary command. Callers need an integration that obeys the decision before action release.

Sources: wishlist lifecycle, backend launch, operator authentication.

6. Reports and closeout compile the campaign state#

Reports read stored evidence, findings, coverage, runtime material, capabilities, and unresolved work. A current report has an explicit workbench object identifier. The report assembly path can refuse a structural replacement that loses populated technical sections. This preserves accumulated explanation while the underlying research continues.

Closeout examines the campaign through a separate gate. Open obligations, missing required receipts, unproved finding states, expired claims, missing context, and stale reports can block the closed result. Coverage below the default 95-percent threshold is advisory. Draft and current report objects can exist before closeout succeeds.

The distinction makes a useful report and a completed campaign separately visible. The operator can resolve the blocking work or record an explicit exception for identified checks. The exception remains linked to its decision record.

Sources: report inputs, replacement protection, closeout checks.

A continuation example#

Consider a source campaign that has characterized a parser and recorded a concrete reproduction lead. The current worker stops after saving an analysis artifact.

  1. The loop preserves available observations and records the failed invocation.
  2. A recoverable failure can receive a bounded replacement attempt.
  3. An unresolved proof or authority question remains a pending action.
  4. The manager reads the stored evidence and selects the next eligible work.
  5. The replacement worker receives the subject context, target, objective, and prior-work instructions.
  6. It extends the evidence and proposes any necessary finding transition.
  7. The backend evaluates the transition receipt independently of the new narrative.
  8. Reports reuse the accumulated state, and closeout checks the remaining obligations.

Changing a configured worker provider does not replace the subject's evidence identifiers, finding history, or module progress. A resumed coordinator can recover saved active conversations and progress. Supported resume checks compare recorded inputs before continuing active work. The detailed continuation behavior and its activation conditions are in Control in depth.

The distinctive contribution#

REFALL connects retained technical knowledge with the machinery that selects the next research task. Coverage, claims, evidence, decisions, and obligations participate in the same continuing campaign. This gives the operator a practical explanation of what was examined, what supports a conclusion, and what should happen next.

ARA, BRA, and REFALL apply related Ready Armor principles through separate implementations. ARA addresses agent runtime and capability composition. BRA addresses governed assessment operations and materialization. REFALL addresses persistent research coordination, evidence acceptance, and campaign completion.

Its contribution is that connected research lifecycle. The model supplies analysis, tools supply observations, and the campaign retains the records needed to continue and review the work.

Read Research cycles for scheduling and stopping behavior. Read Ledger and wishlist for the persistent resource and evidence paths. Read Control in depth for each actual decision boundary.

FIELD GUIDE / 0313 MIN READ

REFALL AB research cycles#

REFALL coordinates a campaign through repeated scheduling cycles and bounded worker conversations. The campaign owns the context, evidence, progress, findings, and unresolved decisions. A worker owns one assignment for one conversation.

These loops have different purposes. A scheduling cycle examines available work and running conversations. A module pass examines a particular subject, unit, or finding. A retry attempts to repair a failed invocation. Report and supervision cycles examine the accumulated campaign state.

Campaign, cycle, and conversation#

TermMeaning
CampaignPersistent research state for a subject workbench.
Standing loopThe coordinator that selects, dispatches, polls, and records work.
Scheduling cycleOne complete pass through the coordinator's main loop.
Worker conversationA bounded request sent to Agent Canvas/OpenHands.
Module passA declared research activity on one target.
RetryA replacement conversation for the same assignment after a recoverable failure.
Pending actionA stored obligation with a status, owner, and applicable receipt requirements.
CloseoutA separate decision about whether campaign records support completion.

The default coordinator has no fixed cycle limit: max_cycles=0. It still returns when its idle conditions are met. It does not wait indefinitely for an operator to add future work.

A finite cycle limit bounds coordinator passes. It does not cancel every conversation when the limit is reached. The coordinator can return running with active conversations saved for continuation. The backend Update operation requests one coordinator cycle. Its Start operation requests an unrestricted cycle count.

Source: standing-loop execution, backend Start and Update.

One scheduling cycle#

Startup loads saved active conversations, the iteration count, and campaign progress. The coordinator loads source identity and performs applicable resume checks. A returned preflight refusal for saved active work produces resume_blocked before new scheduling. When coverage is empty, source enumeration can establish the initial units. The loop then records its running manifest.

Each cycle performs this sequence:

  1. Read coverage and gate state.
  2. Fill available worker slots according to scheduling priority.
  3. Poll every active conversation, including newly dispatched workers.
  4. Process terminal outcomes or ingest available output from running workers.
  5. Update determinations and applicable reports.
  6. Consider report and visualization workers.
  7. Save active conversations, cycle state, and progress.
  8. Evaluate the cycle limit, stall condition, and idle conditions.
  9. Wait for the configured poll interval when another cycle is needed.

Global parallelism defaults to four conversations. The poll interval defaults to five seconds. These are coordinator settings rather than a guarantee about every tool process that a worker can create.

A terminal conversation increments the loop's completed counter. That counter includes failed conversations. Use coverage, module progress, finding state, and pending actions to assess research completion.

Source: cycle body and return conditions.

What receives the next available slot#

The scheduler uses this priority order:

PriorityWorkSelection rule
1Worker-claimable pending actionsClaim eligible open actions or expired leases.
2Requested threat-model workRequire the necessary context and inventory inputs.
3Subject modulesSelect eligible identification, research, toolchain, or synthesis work.
4Fresh coverageClaim an open or expired coverage unit for characterization.
5Finding modulesSelect verification or patch work for registered finding targets.
6Later unit modulesDeepen units already recorded as characterized.

Priority applies whenever the coordinator selects another task. A worker already running a lower-priority assignment is not interrupted merely because higher-priority work appears.

Subject modules can run before fresh coverage. Their own local priority determines which eligible subject module is selected. A subject synthesis module therefore does not automatically wait for all unit review work. Declare the intended prerequisites rather than treating pack names as global phases.

Fresh coverage precedes finding modules and later unit passes. This spreads initial examination across available source units before repeated depth on an early subset. Pending actions still provide a route to urgent validation before ordinary breadth.

Source: dispatch priority, module selection.

Pending work is a queue with ownership#

Pending selection accepts open actions and claimed actions whose leases have expired. It orders candidates by priority, action kind, and recorded time. At equal priority, live validation precedes an ordinary operator-decision action.

Some obligations remain manager work. The worker selector excludes watchdog-stop reviews. It also excludes specified finding-promotion reviews that require manager examination or identify an inventory mismatch. The operator can still see these obligations even when workers have nothing eligible to claim.

A pending-action worker receives the obligation and its required result. Successful processing attempts to resolve it through the pending-action API. Required receipt types and evidence still apply at that API boundary. An unresolved action can remain a closeout blocker after the coordinator becomes idle.

Coverage claims have a separate lease. The backend selects open units or expired claims and updates ownership within a database transaction. The default coverage lease is 900 seconds. An expired claim makes the unit eligible for another claim; it is not successful completion.

Sources: pending selection, worker exclusions, coverage claims.

Depth develops per target#

Module dependencies apply to the same target. A completed pass on parser.py does not satisfy a dependency for writer.py. The scheduler stores completed module identifiers separately for each target.

With no explicit module configuration, the registry selects security_assessment. Its dependency resolution also loads baseline characterization. The built-in source sequence is:

Characterization records the unit in scheduler progress and unlocks dependent passes. Coverage submission has its own acceptance branch. Module progress and recorded coverage therefore answer different questions.

Other packs add different paths:

PackBuilt-in target path
reverse_engineeringSubject identification; unit characterization → decomposition → review.
security_assessmentCharacterization → reconnaissance → review; finding verification.
dynamic_testingCharacterization → harness drafting → runtime verification.
developmentCharacterization → harness drafting; finding patch proposal.
static_analysisSubject toolchain work; characterization → unit review.
researchSubject research and subject synthesis, selected by their local priorities.

Eligible later passes apply completed-work checks, dependencies, active-target checks, applicable path filters, and module concurrency. Fresh characterization uses direct coverage claims instead of that eligibility function. It attaches the first active breadth module and uses the fixed characterize task class. Later unit selection supplies the recorded path but does not supply unit_state. Read Work modules for the configuration fields and their actual selection branches.

Sources: built-in packs, default registry, per-target progress, eligibility.

Findings create another research frontier#

Finding modules operate on registered finding identifiers. The scheduler retains a compact identifier, path, and title for each such target. Completion processing registers finding outputs that contain identifiers. A finding also has canonical evidence, validation, and disposition records outside this scheduling index. Registration in that compact index does not establish that the canonical finding admission gate accepted the candidate.

sec_verify asks a worker to attempt reproduction. Its requested result includes exact steps, expected behavior, observed behavior, and proof status. dev_patch asks for a minimal, verifiable proposed change. Those objectives define assignments; they do not prove reproduction or apply a patch automatically.

When both built-in finding modules are eligible, verification has priority 20 and patch work has priority 70. The built-ins do not declare a patch-to-verification dependency. A patch proposal therefore does not automatically reopen the completed verification module. Use an explicit pending action or a distinct configured verification pass for another examination.

A proposed finding status or quality change passes through typed transitions. Live validation, false-positive decisions, duplicates, downgrades, and deferred chains require their respective receipts. A refused transition preserves the existing finding state and records the refusal. Research can continue while the missing proof or decision remains visible.

Sources: finding registration and selection, finding assignment, transition application, disposition gate.

Evidence arrives before an assignment is complete#

Running conversations can contribute facts, leads, findings, flows, and saved artifacts. The loop reads conversation events and workspace submission files during polling. Stable identities prevent repeated ingestion from producing the same stored observation repeatedly. A failed backend write remains eligible for a later persistence attempt.

Terminal handling uses a specific order:

  1. Classify the invocation status and terminal submission contract.
  2. Parse the output and assignment metadata.
  3. Check whether the structured submission was already applied.
  4. Preserve available research observations.
  5. Handle the classified completion, failure, retry, or operator obligation.

A duplicate applied submission returns before terminal salvage. For other terminal results, salvage precedes failure handling and retry dispatch. A failed conversation can therefore retain useful research without receiving successful assignment completion.

The successful branch applies proposed transitions and persists control requests. Coverage submission additionally requires the exact finished status, a characterization task, and an eligible parsed coverage result. Later modules do not resubmit breadth coverage.

The empty-output guard applies to module tasks that carry no unit record. It requires canonical facts, leads, findings, or flows and successful persistence before module completion. The current subject and finding dispatch shapes use that guard. A completion message alone does not satisfy it.

Sources: incremental ingestion, terminal processing, empty-output guard.

Repetition, retry, and exhaustion#

Built-in modules normally use once_per_target=true. A completed module is then excluded for that target. The active-target check also avoids another instance of that same once-per-target pass while it runs.

Setting once_per_target=false removes those particular exclusions in eligible module selection. Such subject, finding, or later unit passes can become eligible repeatedly. Dependencies, applicable filters, and concurrency settings still affect selection. This is an explicit repeated-work configuration rather than an automatic new research hypothesis.

Invocation retry is a separate mechanism. The classifier defaults to two total attempts for recoverable worker failures. Strict terminal-contract refusal requires REFALL_REQUIRE_STRUCTURED_SUBMIT=true; that setting defaults to false. Claude lane A can fail over to Codex lane B; lane B remains on B. The replacement retains the assignment, module target, and accumulated campaign evidence.

Recognized capability, scope, operator-stop, and tool-execution failures do not use ordinary automatic retry. Capability failures create an access request and decision obligation. Scope failures create an obligation requiring a scope decision receipt. Other exhausted or nonretryable outcomes produce manager-visible review work.

A failed module does not receive successful progress merely because its retry budget ended. It can remain eligible for later scheduling. An expired coverage lease can also expose the original unit again. The invocation retry limit therefore bounds that replacement chain, not every future campaign assignment for the same target.

Sources: eligibility and repetition, failure classification, replacement dispatch, decision obligations.

Reports and visuals have their own cadence#

The default draft refresh interval is ten coordinator cycles. Ordinary assessment refresh requires at least one finding ledger entry. Mapping-mode refresh can instead use recorded facts, leads, flows, or artifacts.

A report-writing conversation uses a different trigger. By default, it needs an available slot, the source-coverage completion predicate, and 30 new facts, leads, or findings. That predicate compares completed and total file counts when both are available. If those counts are absent, it returns true. A nonpositive report threshold disables the default report-worker trigger.

The optional continuous report policy reserves one slot and replaces completed report workers without the default volume trigger. This policy can keep reporting activity available after ordinary analysis work is exhausted.

Visualization is considered every 20 cycles. It requires the source-coverage predicate, an available slot, and the configured resolved-coverage threshold. The default threshold is 25 percent. Ordinary assessment also requires three finding entries; mapping mode uses its separate objective without that finding-count condition.

Worker requestDefault iteration limit
Characterization, subject modules, finding modules, and later unit passes30
Report worker25
Visualization worker20
Replacement retry30

These limits are sent to Agent Canvas with the conversation request. They do not establish campaign closeout or a host-wide resource ceiling.

Sources: draft cadence, report-worker trigger, visualization trigger, conversation request.

Idle, stalled, supervised, and closed#

An idle coordinator has no active conversations under its return conditions. The loop also examines remaining module work and worker-claimable pending actions before an idle exit after dispatch activity. Idle does not mean that every obligation is resolved. Manager-only actions, refused transitions, or missing report proof can still block closeout.

The stall check measures cycles since the most recent terminal conversation. Its default threshold is 36 cycles, with a strict greater-than comparison. A terminal failure updates that completion clock too. The threshold is therefore not a measure of scientific progress or successful proof. A stall return can retain active conversations and report running.

The watchdog supplies another observation and response cycle. It samples services, active conversations, progress signatures, reported usage, and failure signals. With enforcement active, selected conditions can delete a managed conversation and create stop-review records. Its sampled thresholds are separate from per-conversation iteration limits.

The watchdog also examines resource requests in the wishlist. It can recognize an already installed tool or use a configured allowlisted installer when installation is enabled. Unsupported or failed requests remain reported as unhandled work. A wishlist record does not itself grant live execution authority.

The supervisor has fast liveness and full watchdog/status modes. Its default cron entries request a fast pass each minute and a full pass every three minutes. Service recovery can restart the configured backend or Agent Canvas. An absent loop with otherwise healthy services is reported as idle; that branch does not automatically launch a new research loop. Repeated service recoveries can trigger a hold and stop the coordinator process until an operator clears the fault.

Closeout remains a separate operation. It checks pending actions, finding proof, transition receipts, expired claims, stored context, and report freshness. Coverage below the default 95-percent threshold is advisory rather than blocking. The manager can resolve the underlying work or record an explicit, receipted exception for identified checks. Read Control in depth for the gate and authority boundaries.

Sources: return and stall conditions, watchdog pass, wishlist handling, supervisor tick, closeout gate.

Examine a campaign's next step#

  1. Read the stored context, scope, and source inventory.
  2. Inspect active conversations and the last recorded cycle.
  3. Examine worker-claimable obligations before ordinary coverage work.
  4. Check remaining fresh units and expired claims.
  5. Compare each target's completed modules with its dependencies.
  6. Inspect finding verification, patch proposals, and required receipts separately.
  7. Review failed invocations and distinguish their retry chain from later rescheduling.
  8. Inspect the ledger, artifacts, determinations, and report freshness.
  9. Evaluate closeout independently of the coordinator's idle or running status.

Use End-to-end workflows for the operating sequence. Use Technical codex for the broader implementation path.

FIELD GUIDE / 0412 MIN READ

Evidence ledger and resource wishlist#

REFALL AB keeps research results and resource needs with the subject workbench. The evidence ledger preserves findings, facts, leads, decisions, and operational history. The wishlist records missing tools, environments, dependencies, access, and data. Together, these records help the next worker continue useful work with the resources already available.

A ledger entry records what happened or what the research supports. A wishlist item records what a researcher needs. A pending action records an obligation for a worker or manager. A capability request asks for permission to perform a scoped action. These records have separate APIs and lifecycles.

Select the correct record#

NeedRecordResult
Preserve a source fact or a possible research path.Ledger fact or lead.Later workers and reports can reuse the evidence.
Preserve a proposed vulnerability.Ledger finding and the coverage finding API.The evidence history and finding lifecycle remain available.
Request a missing executable or analysis environment.Wishlist item.The watchdog or operator can examine the need.
Track work that must receive a decision or receipt.Pending action.Eligible actions enter the standing loop before ordinary coverage work.
Request a live action outside current permissions.Capability request.An operator can grant the necessary scoped capability.
Record a grant, refusal, transition, or exception.Corresponding decision API.The API updates its own state and appends a ledger record.

The ledger accepts rich JSON records. Its append route validates the entry kind, rather than the complete evidence contract. Use the finding, disposition, capability, and pending-action APIs for their state changes. Appending a ledger entry alone does not perform those changes. See evidence procedures and Control in Depth.

Source: ledger append, pending action creation, and finding persistence.

Evidence ledger#

Storage and entry fields#

Each workbench has a refall_ledger.jsonl file beneath its storage directory. Each nonempty line contains one JSON entry. The append API writes a new line and records a storage audit event.

FieldBehavior
kindDefaults to fact. The value must be a supported kind.
idDefaults to a new identifier with the led_ prefix.
workbench_slugDefaults to the slug from the route.
created_atDefaults to the current UTC timestamp.
updated_atReceives the current UTC timestamp on append.
Other fieldsRemain in the JSON entry.

Useful evidence fields include title, summary, evidence, confidence, limitations, source_anchors, and artifact_refs. Use lane, severity, subject, agent, and unit_id when they identify the work. Preserve exact source references and artifact identifiers. Record secret presence without the secret value.

The supported kinds are:

  • fact, lead, finding, observation, and hypothesis.
  • remediation, attack-chain, ask, coverage, validation, and artifact.
  • ops-event, disposition-transition, and pending-action.
  • capability-grant, capability-request, and capability-decision.
  • runtime-event and closeout-gate.

Source: entry kinds and storage.

Append, correction, and order#

The ledger API exposes append, list, lookup, and statistics operations. It has no entry update or delete route. To correct a result, append a new entry with a new identifier. Include the earlier identifier and explain the correction. Use the relevant state API when the correction changes a finding or decision.

List responses preserve file order. The implementation generates no numeric sequence, previous-entry hash, or ledger hash chain. created_at can come from the submitted record. Use the entry identifier to cite evidence, rather than treating its timestamp as a trusted sequence number.

A repeated caller-supplied identifier can produce multiple lines. Lookup by identifier returns the first matching entry. A repeated append is therefore not an update operation.

Source hashes serve a different purpose. Receipts can carry source_hashes, and the run manifest records source and configuration hashes. Those hashes identify input bytes; they do not authenticate the JSONL ledger.

Source: append and lookup, evidence receipts, and manifest hashes.

Other ledger files#

Subject bootstrap also creates .refall/evidence_ledger.json with an empty entries array. The workbench ledger API uses refall_ledger.jsonl instead. Runtime events and checkpoints have their own storage and APIs. Use the workbench ledger routes for shared evidence and decisions.

Source: subject bootstrap and ledger path.

Read before work#

  1. Read the stored subject context and scope.
  2. Read the coverage summary for the assigned unit.
  3. Read prior facts, leads, and findings for that unit.
  4. Examine referenced artifacts and saved analysis.
  5. Extend the evidence and record the new result.

The standing loop puts these reuse instructions in objectives for later unit modules. They tell workers to use prior coverage, ledger records, and the shared blackboard. This is worker guidance; the ledger API does not enforce a mandatory read before a write.

The loop also ingests evidence during active conversations and at completion. It reads tagged output and saved workspace results. Its in-memory identity set suppresses repeated facts, leads, findings, and flows during that run. A backend failure removes staged identities so a later attempt can retry persistence. This process does not add a general deduplication rule to the ledger API.

Flow evidence uses kind: "fact" with fact_kind: "flow" and a nested flow object. The loop separately submits findings to the coverage finding store. Finding promotion can refuse a candidate even when its ledger evidence remains available.

Source: reuse instructions, incremental ingestion, ingestion identities, and entry conversion.

Read and append through the API#

Set REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the backend address. Set REFALL_WORKBENCH to an existing workbench slug. The examples use a fictional source file and artifact identifier.

bash
export REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:7673"
export REFALL_WORKBENCH="example"

curl -fsS "$REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/api/workbenches/$REFALL_WORKBENCH/ledger/stats"

curl -fsS --get \
  "$REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/api/workbenches/$REFALL_WORKBENCH/ledger/entries" \
  --data-urlencode 'kind=fact' \
  --data-urlencode 'lane=source-review'

curl -fsS -X POST \
  "$REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/api/workbenches/$REFALL_WORKBENCH/ledger/entries" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{
    "kind": "fact",
    "subject": "example",
    "lane": "source-review",
    "unit_id": "unit-example",
    "title": "Configuration reaches the parser",
    "summary": "The loader passes the configuration to parse_config.",
    "evidence": "The call passes the loaded byte buffer.",
    "confidence": "high",
    "limitations": ["Runtime behavior was not examined."],
    "source_anchors": ["src/config.py:42"],
    "artifact_refs": ["artifact-example"]
  }'

The append response contains the entry identifier. Use it with GET /api/workbenches/{slug}/ledger/entries/{entry_id}.

RouteResult
POST /api/workbenches/{slug}/ledger/entriesAppends an entry; returns HTTP 201.
GET /api/workbenches/{slug}/ledger/entriesLists entries in file order.
GET /api/workbenches/{slug}/ledger/entries/{entry_id}Returns the first matching entry, or HTTP 404.
GET /api/workbenches/{slug}/ledger/statsReturns totals by kind, lane, and severity.

List filters are kind, lane, severity, and since. The first three use exact matches. since compares the stored created_at strings with the supplied value. Use consistent UTC timestamp formats for time queries. An unsupported kind returns HTTP 422.

Source: ledger routes and list filters.

Interface and report use#

Open the workbench Ops panel and select Ledger. The panel shows the latest 80 appended entries in reverse file order. Each row shows its title, kind, timestamp, status, provider or lane, and summary when available. Select Output to examine facts, leads, and findings with source or artifact references. Use the API for the complete ledger.

Report drafting reads ledger entries, ledger statistics, coverage, runtime evidence, pending actions, and capability state. Report enrichment also reads the stored ledger. The report combines recorded evidence; a narrative alone does not perform finding verification.

Source: Ledger view, Output filters, report drafting, and report enrichment.

Resource wishlist#

Workbench records#

The current coverage client defaults to workbench coverage. Its wishlist records reside in the workbench refall_coverage.db database.

FieldPurpose
idRequest identifier. The backend generates a wish_ identifier when absent.
subjectSubject name. The route slug supplies the default.
kindResource category, such as tool, env, dep, access, or data.
itemNecessary resource. This field must be nonempty.
reasonWork that the resource will support.
requested_byResearcher or operator identifier.
statusDefaults to open; provided identifies delivery records.
created_at, updated_atDatabase timestamps.

kind and status are string fields rather than fixed enums. The automation specifically interprets open and provided. A custom status does not introduce an automatic workflow.

The workbench API creates rows and lists them. It exposes no wishlist update or resolve route. A delivery record is a new row with status: "provided". Keep the original request identifier in its reason or in a related ledger entry.

Source: wishlist request fields, database operations, and client mode.

Record and examine a request#

  1. Check the provided list before requesting a resource.
  2. Name one resource and the work it will support.
  3. Create an open wishlist item.
  4. Examine watchdog results or arrange operator provision.
  5. Record delivery and verify availability in the worker environment.
  6. Obtain any necessary capability grant before live use.
bash
curl -fsS --get \
  "$REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/api/workbenches/$REFALL_WORKBENCH/coverage/wishlist" \
  --data-urlencode 'status=provided'

curl -fsS -X POST \
  "$REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/api/workbenches/$REFALL_WORKBENCH/coverage/wishlist" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{
    "kind": "tool",
    "item": "exiftool",
    "reason": "Read metadata from the assigned sample files.",
    "requested_by": "research-worker",
    "status": "open"
  }'

curl -fsS --get \
  "$REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/api/workbenches/$REFALL_WORKBENCH/coverage/wishlist" \
  --data-urlencode 'status=open'

Both list requests can also use subject. The backend lists matching rows by updated_at, newest first. There is no separate automatic approval state in this wishlist API.

For manual provision, create another row through the same POST route. Set status to provided and identify the original request in reason. For example, a delivered test environment can use this body:

json
{
  "kind": "env",
  "item": "isolated parser environment",
  "reason": "Provided for request wish-example; use the assigned worker environment.",
  "requested_by": "operator",
  "status": "provided"
}

This row records delivery. Configure the worker environment separately before its next task.

Source: wishlist routes.

Watchdog provision#

When the watchdog runs, it collects the workbench's open and provided wishlist rows. It normalizes the first token of each resource name to an executable name. It skips names already represented in the provided list.

For an eligible request, it first checks shutil.which on the watchdog host. If the executable exists, the watchdog records delivery. Otherwise, an enabled installation path can use the fixed Homebrew commands below.

Requested executableHomebrew package
binwalkbinwalk
exiftoolexiftool
radare2 or r2radare2
rizin or rz-binrizin
yarayara

The eligible categories are tool, cli, binary, package, dependency, or an empty kind. The installation setting defaults to enabled. Without an explicit watchdog configuration, REFALL_WATCHDOG_INSTALL_WISHLIST controls that setting. REFALL_WATCHDOG_WISHLIST_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_S defaults to 900 seconds. An explicit WatchdogConfig supplies its own installation values.

A successful command must also make the executable discoverable through shutil.which. The watchdog then creates a new provided row. It appends an ops-event with action watchdog.wishlist.provided. The event links the request and delivery identifiers and includes an availability or installation receipt. The original open row remains unchanged. Thus, an open count can include a request that already has a separate delivery record.

Dry-run mode skips installation and returns proposed delivery records without writing them. Unsupported categories, disabled installation, missing installers, and failed installation appear in the result's unhandled list. A host executable check establishes availability on the watchdog host. Check its path or mount separately before use inside a worker container or remote environment.

Source: installer table, configuration, provision decisions, and delivery receipt.

Delivered resources reach agents#

The head orchestrator reads provided items during each cycle. It inserts them into the specialist objective under DELIVERED WISHLIST ITEMS. The research, binary research, binary review, and binary validation drivers also insert this information into their prompts. They tell workers to check delivered resources before requesting duplicates. A failed provided-list read returns an empty list in the shared helper.

The standing loop uses a separate scheduler. It does not directly turn wishlist rows into tasks or insert the shared delivered-item block. Its pending-action path selects claimable obligations before ordinary research modules. Some review actions remain manager work and are excluded from worker dispatch.

Source: head cycle, prompt formatter, research driver, binary drivers, scheduler order, and manager-only exclusions.

Compatibility dashboard#

The separate coverage service retains its own wishlist API and SQLite store. Its subject dashboard shows wishlist items and a provided button for open items. That button calls POST /wishlist_resolve and updates the existing row. This differs from the workbench API's separate delivery row.

Compatibility routeBehavior
POST /wishlistCreates an open item with subject, item, optional kind, reason, and requested_by.
GET /wishlist?subject=example&status=providedLists matching items; the store returns at most 500.
POST /wishlist_resolveUpdates an existing row from a body with id and status.

Use these routes only with the standalone coverage service. They operate on that service's database, rather than automatically mirroring workbench rows. The native workbench Ops panel provides ledger, pending-action, and capability controls. It does not provide this compatibility wishlist button.

Source: compatibility routes, update behavior, and dashboard action.

From a resource need to completed work#

Consider a worker that needs metadata extraction and later needs a live network check.

  1. The worker reads earlier evidence and the provided wishlist.
  2. It records an open exiftool request with the research reason.
  3. The watchdog finds the host executable or uses its configured installation path.
  4. The watchdog writes a delivery row and a ledger receipt.
  5. A supported head or driver prompt includes the delivered tool on its next dispatch.
  6. The worker checks tool availability in its execution environment and records source or artifact evidence.
  7. The worker requests a scoped capability before the live network action.
  8. The operator examines the capability request and supplies an appropriate grant.
  9. The supported execution path requests authorization for the intended action.
  10. The worker submits the result and resolves related pending work with the necessary receipt.

A provided wishlist item records resource availability, rather than permission to use that resource against any target. A capability grant carries the class, scope, expiry, and execution conditions used by the authorization decision. Operator-token authentication applies to capability mutations when the deployment configures that credential. The decision API records its result; it does not execute an arbitrary submitted command. See execution boundaries.

A direct capability_missing failure can create a capability request and an operator-decision pending action. A direct scope_blocked failure can create a pending action with a scope_decision receipt type. Neither path creates a wishlist item automatically. The operator can track a related resource need in the wishlist and keep the decision in its own queue. A capability grant creates a separate grant record; it does not update the request row or a wishlist item.

Source: failure routing, capability API, and pending-action receipt routes.

REFALL AB feature catalog#

REFALL organizes research into persistent subjects, bounded execution, evidence, decisions, and deliverables. These features work together around one subject workbench.

Subject workbench#

Each subject has metadata, a source path, a storage path, context, and a theme. Coverage, ledger entries, pending actions, capabilities, and reports belong to the same workbench. The operator can inspect the research without reconstructing it from terminal history.

The Ops panel presents Context, scope, threat model, live agent state, coverage, runtime records, and closeout information. It can generate or save context, request a threat model, run diagnosis, estimate work, and issue lifecycle commands. Pending actions can be resolved, deferred, or cancelled with receipts. Capability requests and grants remain visible beside the research.

Source: WorkbenchOpsPanel.

Research ledger and Output projection#

The subject ledger records facts, leads, findings, validation, artifacts, decisions, and operational events. Its API appends JSONL records and supplies filtered lists, individual entries, and summary statistics. The Ops Ledger view exposes the history. The Output view filters research records and expands their evidence, next steps, and worker identifiers. Reports read the ledger together with coverage and runtime state.

The ledger preserves evidence history. Finding, capability, and pending-action APIs perform their corresponding state transitions. Read Ledger and wishlist for exact entry fields and route examples.

Resource requests and delivery#

The wishlist records missing tools, dependencies, access, and other research needs. The watchdog reads open and provided records. For supported executable requests, it checks host availability and can use its configured fixed installer list. Delivery appends a provided row and a linked ledger receipt. The original request stays in history.

Head cycles read the delivered resources before preparing objectives. The research driver and three binary drivers include a provided-item snapshot loaded at startup. Their prompts tell workers to use delivered items before requesting duplicates. The standing loop selects pending actions, coverage units, and work modules through separate queues. Read the delivery lifecycle.

Connected research cycles#

Campaign polling, module passes, worker retries, reporting, and supervision have separate triggers and state. A coordinator cycle can ingest observations from a still-active worker. A terminal result preserves useful evidence before handling the classified outcome or scheduling retry. Per-target dependencies permit different components to advance at different rates. Read Research cycles for the priorities, limits, and feedback paths.

Shared context and readiness#

Context generation collects subject metadata, source material, workbench text, and operator direction. The selected provider produces a Markdown briefing. REFALL stores the briefing in a workbench object, subject file, and coverage context record. The backend refuses a start request without stored context.

Doctor examines services, provider commands, paths, context, capabilities, secrets presence, and relevant tooling. Estimate combines inventory size, remaining coverage, pending actions, and readiness. Its task count helps the operator plan the run.

Source: Context and readiness operations.

File identity and coverage#

The inventory records relative paths, SHA-256 hashes, file sizes, line counts, and detected kinds. It streams file content without a fixed file-size ceiling. It records unreadable files and relevant symlink observations. Scanner exclusions keep dependencies and generated runtime state outside ordinary inventory.

Coverage units divide files into symbols or line ranges. Claims use leases so interrupted workers do not retain permanent ownership. A successful characterization stores a summary, sensitivity, data touched, incoming flows, outgoing flows, and leads. The coverage view can then answer both what was examined and what the examiner learned.

A resolved percentage measures recorded characterization and dead-code dispositions. It is distinct from vulnerability proof and behavioral completeness. Binary-only intake requests an explicit analysis plan instead of inventing line coverage.

Sources: Inventory, coverage store.

Composable work modules#

A module declares its task class, target source, dependencies, selection rules, priority, and execution limits. Its target can be the entire subject, an examined coverage unit, or a finding. A dependency applies to the same target rather than imposing a global phase on every worker.

Seven packs supply characterization, reverse engineering, security assessment, research, development, dynamic examination, and static analysis. Custom declarations can add subject-specific work without a new core driver. Path filters focus later unit passes on recorded component paths. Per-module limits control subject, finding, and later unit selection. Fresh characterization uses coverage claims and the global loop concurrency limit. That breadth path attaches the first active breadth module without applying module path filters.

The default selection enables security assessment and its characterization prerequisite. An explicit baseline selection supports a characterization-focused campaign. Read Work modules for configuration examples.

Source: Module registry and scheduler.

Specialist routing#

The router maps task classes to specialist lanes and verification expectations. Claude normally handles research, interpretation, review, and synthesis. Codex normally handles enumeration, tooling, harness creation, patching, and verification. A subject lane pattern can distribute configured providers across active slots.

Optional Grok work uses a host-managed sandbox configuration. The manager transfers permitted subject material and records accepted results through REFALL. It has a separate execution role from the normal Claude and Codex Agent Canvas lanes.

Sources: Router, lane configuration.

Continuous evidence capture#

Agent output can occur in messages, action text, structured submission files, or saved analysis files. REFALL reads these channels during the run. A specialist can therefore contribute useful observations before its final response.

Incremental ingestion and terminal processing share stable evidence identities. This prevents the same fact from appearing again on each poll. If the backend cannot persist an item, its identity remains eligible for a later attempt.

At termination, the loop classifies the invocation and parses its output. It checks submission identity and preserves observations before handling the classified outcome. A stopped worker can leave valuable evidence while its assigned task remains unfinished. A subject module with no durable observations creates pending work instead of a false success.

Source: Evidence capture.

Structured results#

The refall.submit.v1 schema separates task results, findings, evidence changes, control requests, and threat models. Evidence-bearing results carry confidence, limitations, and source anchors or artifact references. Nested findings require concrete locations. Stable submission identifiers prevent repeated application of terminal results.

The parser also accepts legacy facts, leads, flows, coverage markers, and finding blocks. Strict mode makes a missing or malformed structured result a pending obligation. The loop can fill assignment metadata that it already knows. It does not create missing source proof.

Sources: Submission parser, typed contracts.

Findings and decisions#

A candidate finding must supply evidence, confidence, and a source or artifact location. The promotion gate checks source references against the inventory when that inventory is available. It checks external hosts against explicit scope. A claimed validation result requires verification material.

Finding identity uses the subject, vulnerability class, normalized title, and affected component. Repeated locations stay attached to a canonical finding.

Lifecycle state and evidence quality remain separate. An accepted VALID transition requires a live_repro receipt. False-positive, duplicate, deferred, and downgrade decisions also require appropriate receipts. A stale source hash or conflicting pending obligation can refuse the transition. Accepted and refused attempts remain inspectable.

Sources: Promotion gate, finding transitions.

Scoped action authority#

A capability grant identifies an action class, scope, grantor, expiry, and additional conditions. Authorization requests identify the actor, command, target, and declared effects. The broker compares these records before it returns an authorization decision.

Its checks include applicable host, port, HTTP method, filesystem path, expiry, and declared-identity conditions. Grant and revoke authentication requires a configured REFALL_CAPABILITY_OPERATOR_TOKEN_PATH. With the default unset token, the API retains caller-supplied identity fields. It distinguishes network, Docker, Codebadger, secret use, and destructive actions. A destructive grant can require a dry run and an approval token. The production launch path uses this broker before starting the standing loop.

The broker governs requests submitted to its authorization route. That route records a decision without executing the command. Direct worker tools do not automatically pass through it. The execution environment supplies the operating-system and container boundaries for agent processes. Existing mounts supply their configured permissions; the source-copy fallback does not make files read-only. Read Control in depth for the complete boundary model.

Source: Capability matching.

Pending obligations#

Missing capability, blocked scope, incomplete proof, exhausted retries, and unanswered operator decisions become pending actions. An action identifies its source, priority, ownership, status, and required receipt. Workers claim eligible pending work before ordinary coverage units. An operator can resolve, defer, or cancel the action through the workbench.

This makes a blocked result visible work. It also gives later manager sessions an explicit account of what remains unresolved.

Source: Pending action store.

Continuity and supervision#

Loop state preserves active conversations and the current iteration. Module progress preserves completed work for each target. The blackboard supplies compact shared notes. Runtime manifests and checkpoints connect a run to source identities, provider configuration, and stage results. Resume preflight checks recorded input hashes before resumed execution.

Transport retries handle temporary service failures. Worker retries distinguish repairable output from capability, scope, and operator-stop conditions. A retry can switch from Claude to Codex within the configured attempt limit. Successful conversations are archived before cleanup.

The watchdog examines progress, failures, budgets, and service state. The supervisor separates fast liveness checks from broader review. Repeated recovery can produce an operator hold rather than endless restart activity.

Sources: Standing loop, watchdog, supervisor.

Living reports#

The draft combines findings, architecture facts, flows, coverage, runtime proof, pending actions, and capability decisions. Enrichment groups evidence and retains related locations. A report worker can maintain analyst notes alongside the formal deliverable. Report scheduling can use new evidence volume or reserve a continuous report slot.

The current report is an explicitly selected workbench object. Replacement checks protect populated technical sections from a thinner generated report. The operator can inspect a refused replacement candidate separately.

Visual evidence can include graph images, screenshots, captures, CodeCharta data, or focused property-graph slices. The report standards connect these artifacts to their claims and provenance.

Sources: Draft, enrichment, assembly.

Checked closeout#

The closeout gate evaluates unfinished actions, disposition receipts, proof, expired claims, context, and report freshness. It separates blocking failures from advisory warnings. Coverage threshold, high-impact visuals, toolchain use, and disclosure output can produce warnings. Open obligations and a stale report can block completion. An explicit override receipt records an operator exception.

Source: Closeout gate.

FIELD GUIDE / 066 MIN READ

REFALL AB end-to-end workflows#

From subject to research campaign#

1. Attach the subject#

Create a workbench for the selected source tree or material directory. The subject record separates the examined source from the workspace that stores run state and outputs. The workbench receives its own context, coverage, ledger, and report pointer.

bash
python3 -m ref_all_executor subject create example --source-path /absolute/path/to/example

2. Establish shared context#

Generate the briefing through the Context view or named context operation. The context writer receives source material, workbench text, metadata, and operator direction. REFALL stores the resulting Markdown in the backend and subject workspace.

Read the briefing before execution. Use it to define the target, available material, research priorities, constraints, and done conditions.

bash
python3 -m ref_all_executor ops command context example

3. Select the work#

Choose module packs and any subject-specific declarations. Set include or exclude globs for later passes over characterized units. Set the scope overlay and request a threat model when useful. A mapping campaign can select characterization and decomposition without security assessment modules.

4. Check readiness and authority#

Run Doctor to inspect services, provider commands, paths, context, capabilities, and supporting tools. Run Estimate to inspect remaining work and prerequisites. Provide the subject-scoped launch grant through the capability interface. A configured operator token authenticates grant changes; the unset default does not. The browser client does not attach that token automatically. Use an authenticated host-side client when token protection is active.

bash
python3 -m ref_all_executor ops command doctor example
python3 -m ref_all_executor ops command estimate example

5. Start through backend operations#

The web interface and production CLI use the same backend launch path. The backend checks context and authorizes the process request. It then checks Agent Canvas and projects the source into its configured workspace. A matching bind mount can supply the source directly. Otherwise, the source-sync helper copies a snapshot into the container.

bash
python3 -m ref_all_executor loop start example

6. Build the examination surface#

If coverage is empty, the standing loop builds a source inventory. Each included file has a path, content hash, size, kind, and line count. Coverage units form the denominator for recorded examination. A binary-only root opens an analysis-plan action instead of becoming synthetic line coverage.

7. Assign a bounded task#

The scheduler first considers pending actions and requested threat-model work. It then considers subject modules, fresh coverage units, finding modules, and later unit passes. Subject, finding, and later unit selection apply the relevant module eligibility checks. Fresh characterization uses coverage claims and the global loop concurrency limit. It attaches the first active breadth module and its objective.

The task objective contains context, scope, shared notes, target details, routing rationale, and an output contract. The dispatcher adds source, writable workspace, and approved resource information. Agent Canvas starts the selected specialist conversation.

8. Compile observations during execution#

The loop polls execution state and reads agent-authored event messages. It also reads structured submission files and registers saved analysis files. Facts, leads, findings, and flow relationships become durable research records during the run. The workbench can show those results before the conversation ends.

9. Separate evidence from completion#

Terminal handling first classifies the invocation, parses its output, and checks submission identity. It preserves useful observations before handling success, scheduling repair, or creating an operator obligation. Only the characterization success path submits its coverage result. Later modules extend the evidence without submitting that coverage again.

Malformed strict output, missing capability, and blocked scope create pending work. A failed worker does not erase its supported observations. A subject module without durable results does not advance as completed work.

10. Review the finding#

A candidate passes through evidence and source-reference checks. The canonical record preserves equivalent evidence locations. A proposed state change then goes through the disposition gate. Typed receipts explain promotion, rejection, duplicates, deferral, or downgrade. Source-dependent receipts can include hashes for freshness checks.

11. Publish accumulated understanding#

Periodic drafts and report workers compile findings, architecture, flows, proof, and remaining questions. Analyst notes preserve developing understanding separately from the formal report. The current report pointer selects the deliverable visible in the workbench. A structural comparison can refuse a replacement that removes populated technical sections.

12. Close with explicit state#

Prepare the draft and enrichment before requesting closeout. The gate checks open obligations, validation, disposition receipts, expired claims, context, and the current report. It returns individual blocking checks and warnings. Resolve the blocking conditions or record an operator override receipt.

bash
python3 -m ref_all_executor report draft example
python3 -m ref_all_executor report enrich example
python3 -m ref_all_executor loop closeout example

Source and binary workflows#

Main workbench loop#

The main loop uses work modules and workbench-local APIs. It combines subject tasks, coverage breadth, finding tasks, and later examination passes. This is the loop launched by the normal Start and Update operations.

Source investigation driver#

The standalone source family uses coverage_service.tools.seed_subject and drive_research.py. The seed scanner locates concrete source patterns for commands, parsers, files, network access, secrets, and authorization. It groups anchors into prioritized investigation questions.

A researcher claims a question, reads the anchor, traces data, and examines related callers or callees. Concrete leads can add child investigations to the frontier. The driver runs batches until that frontier is exhausted, a configured limit is reached, or the operator stops it. The specialist prompts use the standalone compatibility coverage service.

Binary investigation driver#

The binary family begins with coverage_service.tools.seed_binary. It identifies executable format and imports through radare2. It maps selected dangerous imports to callers and generates function-level investigations.

drive_binresearch.py assigns bounded decompilation work. Workers examine pseudocode, disassembly, arguments, and cross-references. They trace attacker-controlled data to the relevant operation and add concrete branch questions.

drive_binreview.py runs an independent adversarial review of provisional findings. Reviewers reopen the cited function and challenge reachability, bounds checks, mitigations, and severity. They retain exact missing proof targets when a claim remains uncertain.

drive_binvalidate.py selects retained findings without complete runtime proof. Validators prepare a canonical payload, reproduction command, trace, raw output, and observed effect. Subject-specific host actions supply the required execution surface. The driver can publish research visuals and a disclosure package when its validation conditions are satisfied.

These standalone drivers have their own batch lifecycle and compatibility API contracts. They are separate entry points from the module scheduler. Read the driver arguments and subject harness requirements before selecting that family.

Recovery without losing the campaign#

An Update request runs one bounded scheduling and polling cycle. It can resume active conversations from stored loop state. Per-target module progress prevents already completed passes from being repeated unnecessarily.

Resume preflight compares recorded source and lane-configuration hashes. A refused resume remains an explicit decision in runtime and pending state. Temporary HTTP failures use transport retries. Recoverable worker failures use bounded repair attempts. Capability and scope failures request decisions instead of repeated execution.

Conversation trajectories and event streams are archived before successful cleanup. The watchdog and supervisor inspect progress and service health. Recovery restores the failed component within the configured policy. Operator holds preserve visibility when repeated recovery is ineffective.
