REFALL AB technical codex#

This guide traces the implementation from operator intent to stored research, report updates, and checked campaign closeout. Read End-to-end workflows for the operator sequence. Read Work modules for subject configuration. Read Control in depth for each enforcement boundary, guidance layer, default, and exception.

1. Operator controls reach backend operations#

WorkbenchOpsPanel.svelte loads context, scope, threat model, coverage, ledger records, pending actions, capabilities, runtime evidence, and closeout checks. Its lifecycle controls call the named operation API. The Start control requests a subject launch grant through the capability API when needed. Its browser client does not attach an operator token automatically. When token protection is configured, an authenticated host-side client can establish the grant first.

The production CLI uses RefallLoopManager. Its normal start and update methods call backend operations through ArcticBaseClient. The injectable direct launcher supports controlled embedding and focused tests.

The backend run_command route checks whether named operations are enabled. _execute_named_command validates and dispatches the requested command. _start_subject creates or selects the workbench and requires stored context. _update_subject reads the existing subject and requests a bounded pass.

Sources: Ops panel, CLI manager, backend dispatch.

2. Context becomes a shared input#

_context_subject gathers subject material and runs the configured context writer. The writer receives operator direction, metadata, selected source content, and workbench text. Provider command construction is separate from the resulting briefing. The output is Markdown rather than an agent conversation history.

_save_context_artifacts stores the briefing as a subject file and workbench object. The coverage context record mirrors the same research input. The standing loop reads that record when it builds later objectives. The source inventory, scope overlay, and optional threat model remain distinct records.

This separation gives each specialist the same subject identity and declared boundaries. It also lets the operator revise context without reconstructing a worker's private state.

Source: Context generation and persistence.

3. Process launch has an authorization record#

_authorize_process_launch constructs a run_local_command request. It includes the standing-loop argument vector, a declared process effect, the requester, and the subject path. The coverage store compares the request with active capability grants. The backend appends the decision to the workbench ledger. A refused decision returns HTTP 403 before process launch.

The capability matcher checks class, expiry, declared requester and grantor strings, and applicable host, port, method, and path conditions. The token-protected grant route supplies an authenticated operator identity only when its token file is configured. The default unset-token mode retains caller-supplied grantor fields. It also checks declared or recognized network, Docker, Codebadger, secret, and destructive effects. The general authorization route records a decision without executing a command. The backend launch caller obeys refusal; direct worker tools do not automatically pass through that route.

_launch_standing_loop verifies the repository path, prepares the subject projection, and checks Agent Canvas. It starts a detached process with the selected workbench URL and loop limits. Continuous loops can install the configured supervisor schedule. Bounded Update passes run without that continuous-loop schedule.

Sources: Launch authorization, capability matching, launcher.

4. Source projection and scratch state stay separate#

sync_agent_canvas_workspace checks whether a matching Docker mount already supplies the source. When a mount exists, it records its read-only or writable state. Otherwise, it compares a source snapshot marker and copies the source when necessary. The snapshot marker uses file count, total size, and modification information for synchronization.

The inventory supplies separate content hashes for research identity. A synchronization marker and a source hash therefore serve different purposes.

The dispatcher prepares a deterministic writable directory for each assignment. The path includes the subject, lane, task class, and unit identity or objective hash. The objective identifies the scratch workspace and the subject source root separately. An operator can supply a read-only source mount as an execution boundary. The source-copy fallback does not create that restriction. The dispatcher's read-only source statement is model guidance. Process permissions and configured mounts determine actual file access.

Sources: Workspace projection, workspace naming, dispatcher.

5. Inventory establishes identity and examination units#

build_source_inventory walks the subject under explicit exclusion rules. It hashes content in chunks and records size, line count, and kind. Unreadable files remain visible in the skipped list. Symlink observations retain relevant source relationships. Selected configuration directories, such as .github, remain eligible despite their dot prefix.

_auto_enumerate_if_empty stores the inventory and sends file records to coverage enumeration. It runs only when coverage has no recorded lines. A binary-only inventory creates binary_analysis_plan_required instead of synthetic line coverage.

partition_file and build_units turn supplied symbol ranges and uncovered lines into nonoverlapping units. claim_next uses a database transaction to claim an open unit or an expired lease. The default lease is 900 seconds. submit requires file-bearing evidence and writes the characterization fields.

Sources: Inventory builder, automatic enumeration, unit and claim store.

6. Scheduling follows target state#

ModuleRegistry.from_config reads the subject's module declaration. The executable default selects security assessment and resolves its built-in characterization dependency. Custom declarations, disabled identifiers, and overrides then shape the registry. Validation rejects unknown classes, invalid concurrency values, missing dependencies, and dependency cycles.

Subject, finding, and later unit selection use eligible_modules. That function checks supplied target properties, dependencies, completion tracking, active work, and module concurrency. Later unit selection supplies the recorded path from its characterized-unit collection. It does not supply the optional unit_state argument. Finding selection supplies its recorded path when available.

Fresh breadth claims a coverage unit directly. _task_for_characterize attaches the first active breadth module, uses task class characterize, and sets 30 iterations. That branch uses the global concurrency limit rather than module path filters or per-module caps. ModuleScheduler maintains subject, unit, and finding progress. The standing loop then applies its dispatch order.

Pending actions and requested threat models take priority. Subject modules supply foundational research. Fresh coverage units supply breadth. Finding and later unit modules supply additional proof and depth.

A module's after dependency applies to the same target. The scheduler can therefore combine different kinds of work without a single global stage counter.

Sources: Registry, eligibility, claim order.

7. Objective construction carries the contract#

The task builder combines the stored briefing, scope overlay, blackboard, target, module objective, and routing reason. Later unit passes also receive a prior-work instruction. They must examine stored determinations and saved artifacts before extending the analysis. The dispatcher then adds workspace and approved remote-resource information.

The output contract requests facts, leads, findings, flows, determinations, and durable artifacts. A mapping-oriented subject can select the available no-findings contract. That contract preserves architectural observations and leads without treating them as vulnerability findings.

Sources: Task objective, prior-work context, output contracts.

8. Output capture has several entry paths#

An ACP worker can finish on a tool action without a populated final response. read_conversation_agent_text therefore reads the persisted event stream. It collects agent-authored message and action text in order. A final-response request is a fallback.

While a worker runs, _incremental_ingest reads the event stream and workspace. _merge_submission_file accepts structured submission content and embedded research observations. _register_workspace_artifact preserves saved analysis material. All paths converge on parsed findings, facts, leads, and flows.

_persist_new_intel computes stable identities for those records. Incremental ingestion and terminal salvage share the same identity set. A failed backend write removes staged identities so later polling can retry persistence. Persistent submission markers prevent repeated terminal application across retries.

Sources: Event capture, workspace capture, stable persistence.

9. Evidence is retained before outcome handling#

_finish_conversation classifies the invocation and parses the result. It checks persistent submission identity before salvaging observations. It then preserves available research output on both successful and failed outcomes.

A failed outcome saves its output artifact and records retry state. A recoverable failure can launch a bounded repair attempt. Other outcomes create capability, scope, or operator-review obligations.

The clean success path applies transitions and persists control requests. Only a completed characterization task submits its coverage unit. Later passes retain evidence without submitting the breadth result again. A subject module with no canonical observations creates an ingestion-review action and remains incomplete.

Completed conversations save trajectory and event archives before cleanup. A failed archive or cleanup has its own recorded state.

Source: Terminal processing.

10. Claim validation and disposition are separate#

evaluate_finding_candidate examines evidence, confidence, source membership, scope, and claimed validation material. The coverage store then establishes the canonical finding identity and related locations. New findings begin with provisional or research-needed lifecycle state.

transition_finding validates the proposed current and next states. It separately compares evidence-quality tiers. A VALID transition requires a live reproduction receipt. A quality increase requires the corresponding evidence type. Suppression, duplicate decisions, chain deferral, and downgrades have their own receipt rules.

The store refuses stale source hashes and transitions that contradict relevant pending obligations. It records both accepted and refused attempts. The API layer adds the decision to the evidence trail.

Sources: Candidate gate, transition store.

11. Research memory uses explicit records#

RecordResponsibility
Coverage unitExamination identity, lease, determination, evidence, and leads.
Ledger entryFact, lead, finding, validation, artifact, or decision event.
BlackboardCompact shared notes for later tasks.
Module progressCompleted passes and known targets.

ArtifactDurable file content and metadata.

CheckpointStage state and input identities.
Run manifestCurrent providers, source identity, resources, and stage status.

The JSONL ledger records durable evidence and decisions. Runtime SQLite stores events, projections, retries, manifests, and checkpoints. The evidence graph relates those records. Static call graphs remain separate tool outputs.

Resume preflight compares checkpoint input hashes before resumed work. The manifest links source inventory and scope identifiers with the active run. These records support continuity while the active agent or manager changes.

Sources: Runtime store, projection, resume check.

12. Reports compile persistent evidence#

draft_report collects coverage, ledger records, findings, runtime evidence, capabilities, and closeout information. The HTML builder provides detailed finding articles and research sections. The current report identifier is stored in refall_current_report_object_id.

enrich_findings merges equivalent finding locations and groups facts. It also carries runtime observations, artifacts, pending actions, and decisions into the enriched structure. Potential chain groupings remain hypotheses for analyst review.

Before replacement, draft and assembly paths compare populated structural sections. A thinner candidate can be preserved as a diagnostic object while the richer report remains current. This protects architecture, methods, and flow explanations accumulated during earlier research.

The report worker can maintain an analyst-notes artifact alongside the deliverable. The determinations digest records coverage, evidence counts, and module completion counts. Detailed per-unit determinations remain in coverage storage.

Sources: Draft, enrichment, replacement guard.

13. Closeout evaluates the campaign state#

Closeout checks evidence-backed finding decisions, pending obligations, context, claims, proof, and report freshness. A missing or stale current report blocks completion. An open action or a deferred action without its receipt also blocks completion.

Coverage below the configured threshold produces a warning in the closeout gate. The gate also reports advisory visual, toolchain, and disclosure conditions. The blocking field distinguishes these checks from completion barriers. Receipt-backed overrides remain explicit ledger records.

The CLI closeout path drafts, enriches, and refreshes the draft before evaluating the gate. That last refresh includes evidence added during enrichment. It prevents a newly updated evidence trail from leaving the report immediately stale.

Sources: Closeout checks, CLI closeout.

REFALL AB research architecture#

The problem the architecture addresses#

A long research campaign can outlive the conversations that produced its observations. Different workers can examine related code, repeat earlier work, or disagree about what a result proves. A final report then needs an explanation of scope, method, evidence, and unfinished obligations.

REFALL makes the campaign a persistent system of records. The subject owns the evidence. Workers receive bounded assignments and return material that the system can store, compare, and review. The operator retains decisions about scope, live authority, exceptions, and completion.

Three cooperating planes#

Direction and authority#

The operator defines the subject, objective, scope, available resources, and necessary approvals. The manager generates context, selects work, examines progress, and resolves questions. The capability broker evaluates the action requests that pass through its route. The disposition and closeout gates evaluate research decisions and completion state.

Execution#

The standing loop creates bounded tasks and dispatches configured specialists through Agent Canvas/OpenHands. Source tools, decompilers, harnesses, and remote resources supply the relevant examination surface. The selected module determines the purpose of a pass. The execution environment determines the process and container boundary.

Persistent evidence#

The backend stores inventory, coverage, ledger entries, findings, pending actions, capability records, runtime state, artifacts, and report metadata. These records provide input to the next task and the next manager session. The report is a compiled view of this research state.

Ready Armor and control in depth#

Ready Armor public architectures separate what an agent can reason about from what it can authorize. They also separate an agent's action from the evidence supporting its claim. REFALL expresses these principles at the research campaign level.

ConcernREFALL mechanism
What is the assignment?Stored context, scope overlay, target identity, and module objective.
Who owns the work?Coverage claims, pending-action leases, and active task state.
What action is authorized?Scoped capability grants and explicit authorization requests.
What was observed?Facts, flows, artifacts, and source-backed determinations.
What conclusion is supported?Finding promotion checks, quality tiers, and typed transition receipts.
What remains unfinished?Pending actions, refused transitions, validation state, and closeout checks.
What survives the worker?Workbench state, archived events, analyst notes, and reports.

BRA's public architecture focuses on governed assessment execution and materialization. ARA's public architecture focuses on agent runtime policy, engagement composition, procedures, and claim provenance. REFALL focuses on work allocation, research continuity, evidence compilation, report updates, and checked campaign closeout.

The systems share design ideas while retaining separate implementations. REFALL's scheduler, submission parser, ledger, capabilities, and gates are implemented in this repository. Its runtime does not import the ARA or BRA policy engines. A subject-specific ARA mapping contract treats ARA as examined software rather than a runtime dependency.

Build the control stack from actual boundaries#

The lowest REFALL operation prepares resources for the configured execution environment. Source projection validates the input directory and destination subject name. It reuses an existing mount or copies source into the container. The existing mount supplies its actual write restrictions. The copy fallback creates an ordinary container directory.

Inventory then records content identity and source relationships. This record supports later membership and freshness decisions. It does not intercept file access, and an off-root file symlink can still supply inventory content.

The capability broker evaluates requests presented to it. Backend lifecycle operations use that result before loop process release. A refused launch request produces HTTP 403 before the process starts. The general authorization route only returns and records its decision. Other callers must obey that decision before they execute an operation.

Grant and revoke authentication activates with REFALL_CAPABILITY_OPERATOR_TOKEN_PATH. Without that setting, the routes retain supplied identities and do not authenticate an operator token. The matcher compares declared requester and grantor strings. Deployment access control and protected credentials establish the actual operator boundary.

Task selection adds a different control. Dependencies, target progress, applicable path filters, and concurrency rules select later work. Fresh breadth uses direct coverage claims and the global conversation limit. Scope and workspace statements in an objective are instructions to the model. Iteration limits are conversation parameters sent to Agent Canvas. The execution environment supplies the actual filesystem, process, network, and tool permissions.

Continuous capture observes execution and preserves material for subsequent decisions. Finding admission checks evidence references, available inventory membership, and explicit external-target scope. Typed transitions require the appropriate receipt before selected status and quality changes. These are record gates after worker activity; they do not retroactively prevent a tool action.

Closeout checks whether campaign records support a closed lifecycle result. Draft and current report objects can already exist when closeout remains blocked. An explicit exception can make identified failed checks nonblocking while preserving the decision record. The override route records a supplied operator identity without the capability-token authentication dependency.

This stack separates action release, assignment, guidance, observation, and record acceptance. An operator can therefore identify the control that refused a request and the authority needed for a different decision. Read Control in depth for the complete layer model and a worked refusal sequence.

Public background: BRA architecture preview, ARA architecture teaser.

Breadth and depth are distinct research work#

An inventory gives the campaign a measurable starting surface. Characterization records what a unit does and the evidence for that description. Deeper passes can then trace behavior, review trust boundaries, construct harnesses, or verify findings.

The module scheduler prioritizes fresh coverage before repeated deep work on an initial subset. Per-target dependencies still preserve meaningful order within each component. This combination makes broad examination visible while retaining a route to deeper proof.

Recorded coverage is a progress measure. A high percentage does not establish that every behavior is correct or that every possible vulnerability was found. Findings require their own evidence and disposition checks.

Knowledge accumulates in several forms#

A fact describes an observation. A flow describes a relationship between components or data locations. A lead identifies a concrete question and next step. A finding states a supported security issue. A determination summarizes a coverage unit's role, sensitivity, data, and connections.

Artifacts preserve material that would be costly to regenerate. Examples include disassembly, extracted metadata, graph output, traces, payloads, and screenshots. The blackboard gives later tasks compact shared context. Analyst notes retain the evolving architecture and research narrative.

These forms answer different questions. Keeping them separate prevents an open hypothesis from becoming a validated finding through repeated summarization. It also lets architecture mapping produce useful output without manufacturing vulnerabilities.

Completion is a transition#

A worker's termination is an execution event. It is not sufficient evidence that its assigned research is complete. REFALL first classifies the invocation and parses its result. After the submission identity check, it preserves observations before handling the classified outcome.

Structured result validation checks the output envelope and evidence references. Coverage completion requires the appropriate characterization result. A subject module without canonical observations remains unfinished. Capability and scope blocks create operator-visible obligations.

The same principle applies to findings. A false-positive decision, duplicate decision, downgrade, or deferred chain needs a typed receipt. A supported primitive can remain preserved even when standalone exploitability has not been demonstrated.

Source identity matters across time#

The source inventory binds observations to paths and content hashes. A disposition receipt can identify the exact source or configuration bytes that support it. Resume checkpoints record input hashes alongside stage status. The manifest links the active run to inventory and scope records.

This is useful when code changes during an extended campaign. It gives the manager a basis for distinguishing old proof from current material. The current report freshness check also compares publication time with the evidence trail.

Resources are selected for the subject#

The core supplies task generation, result contracts, persistent state, and publication. A subject supplies its source, scope, module configuration, available tools, and necessary execution harnesses.

Source projects can use structural search, semantic navigation, symbol indexes, graphs, and complexity measurements. Binary projects can use decompilation, cross-references, function investigations, and runtime proof. Hardware or platform-specific work requires a configured execution surface and subject harness.

Module declarations add research intent and selection rules. Service definitions add managed tools. Capability grants add authority for specified actions. These are separate configuration decisions.

Models remain execution resources#

Task routing distinguishes reasoning, implementation, review, and verification work. Lane patterns can distribute configured provider capacity. Bounded retries can switch providers when a recoverable worker failure prevents a usable result.

The shared workbench remains the source of research continuity. Replacing a model does not replace the subject inventory, evidence identifiers, pending obligations, or current report. The optional Grok configuration uses a host-managed sandbox with a separate material boundary. Its accepted output returns through the manager.

Evidence graphs and analysis graphs#

The runtime evidence graph relates stored observations and artifact references. It supports review of where claims and outputs came from. Call graphs, dependency graphs, and property graphs describe the examined software. They are generated by the selected analysis tools.

The two graph families complement each other. An analysis graph can explain a code path. The evidence graph can connect that analysis artifact to the research record and resulting conclusion. Neither relationship substitutes for the proof required by a finding's transition.

Reports are maintained research products#

A formal report presents findings, methods, scope, proof, limitations, and remediation. A debrief presents progress, decisions, blockers, and next actions. Analyst notes preserve an evolving technical explanation while the research continues. Visual evidence makes selected paths, relationships, and observed effects easier to examine.

Report generation reads persistent research state. Replacement checks protect populated technical sections from accidental loss. The closeout gate distinguishes unresolved completion barriers from advisory warnings. The operator can therefore see both the campaign result and the conditions under which it was accepted.

REFALL AB control in depth#

REFALL controls a research campaign through several distinct decisions. It selects work, checks brokered authority, captures results, validates record changes, and evaluates completion. Each decision has a defined boundary.

The execution environment controls process permissions, filesystem mounts, network access, and available tools. REFALL supplies campaign coordination and evidence controls above that environment. This separation makes the reason for each refusal visible. It also shows which component must enforce an execution restriction.

Read the layers from resources to decisions#

LayerControl typeDecision or result
Source projectionOperation gateValidate the projection request and prepare the configured container workspace.
InventoryObservationRecord source identity, unreadable files, and symlink relationships.
Capability changesOperator authorityAuthenticate grant and revoke requests when token protection is configured.
Capability matchingPolicy gateAccept or refuse the request presented to the broker.
Backend launchOperation gateRefuse loop process release when authorization fails.
Work selectionTask gateSelect the next eligible assignment and allocate work claims.
Conversation boundsTask gateSend an iteration limit and classify outcomes before retry.
Context and scopeModel guidanceState the assignment, boundaries, resources, and expected evidence.
Resume preflightTask gateCompare checkpoint inputs on supported continuation paths.
Continuous captureObservationPreserve worker results and execution records.
Finding admissionRecord gateCheck evidence references and declared external scope.
Finding dispositionRecord gateCheck typed receipts before status or quality changes.
Pending resolutionRecord gateCheck required receipts for unresolved obligations.
Report replacementRecord gatePreserve populated report sections through the assembly path.
CloseoutRecord gateAccept or block the closed campaign result.
Closeout exceptionsOperator authorityRecord an explicit exception for identified checks.

This order describes responsibility from resources to campaign decisions. A particular command can visit these layers in a different order.

1. Establish the execution resources#

A subject has a host source path and a container source location. The projection helper resolves the host path and requires a directory. It rejects empty subject names, slash-containing names, . and ... It also checks that the configured Agent Canvas container runs. A failed check prevents this synchronization operation from completing.

The helper first looks for a matching Docker mount. When a matching mount exists, the result records its actual read-only or writable mode. Otherwise, the helper copies the source into the container with docker cp. A copied directory has the container's ordinary file permissions. The copy path does not create a read-only mount.

Each dispatched task also receives a separate writable scratch directory. Its name derives from the subject, lane, task class, and unit identity or objective hash. The initial message identifies that directory and instructs the worker to preserve the subject source. Read-only mount configuration supplies mechanical write prevention where that restriction is required.

REFALL does not install a general interceptor around worker shell, network, SSH, or external tool calls. Agent Canvas, container configuration, process credentials, and tool services supply those execution boundaries. The standalone source and binary drivers also depend on their configured execution environments.

Sources: projection, workspace creation, workspace instructions.

2. Record source identity#

The inventory records file paths, hashes, sizes, line counts, and kinds. Unreadable files remain in a skipped-file record. Symlink observations identify relationships that resolve outside the configured root. Directory traversal does not descend through directory symlinks. A file symlink can still supply content through its resolved target.

Inventory collection establishes examination identity. It does not confine later file access. Finding admission can compare source anchors with this inventory. Receipt validation can compare supplied source hashes with the current files. These controls detect record inconsistencies at their respective acceptance points.

Source: inventory and symlink observations.

3. Give capability changes an authenticated operator boundary#

Capability grants define an action class, scope, grantor, expiry, and optional additional requirements. Grant and revoke routes support a host-managed operator token. Set REFALL_CAPABILITY_OPERATOR_TOKEN_PATH to activate this authentication. The request must supply X-REFALL-Operator-Token with the file's token value. Successful authentication sets the grantor to operator. A missing or invalid token gives HTTP 403. An unavailable credential file gives HTTP 503.

The token path defaults to unset. In that mode, grant and revoke routes do not authenticate the operator token. The grant route retains the supplied grantor identity. The browser capability client does not attach the operator token automatically. A protected deployment can issue grants through an authenticated host-side client.

The token file, API reachability, and host-side client belong to the deployment's authority boundary. Restrict their access to the intended operators. String fields such as granted_by and requested_by do not establish authenticated identity by themselves.

Source: operator authentication and capability routes.

4. Evaluate the action presented to the broker#

An authorization request includes a capability class, declared effects, command, requester, and target. The broker requires a class and nonempty effects. It searches active grants of the same class and excludes expired grants. Revoked grants are excluded from that search. No matching grant means refusal.

The matcher applies host and port lists when both the relevant request value and grant restriction exist. A restricted HTTP method requires a matching declared method. A local-command request with a target path requires path scope. Applicable path scope compares the requested target with permitted roots. The matcher uses resolved paths, with a textual containment fallback for resolution errors.

Network, Docker, Codebadger, and secret checks connect applicable effects with their capability classes. Recognized destructive commands require destructive_action. Destructive declarations also activate configured dry-run and approval-token checks. These checks examine declared values and recognized command forms. They are not a complete shell parser or an inspection of every later process effect.

The self-grant rule compares requester and grantor strings. Matching nonoperator strings are refused. The protected grant route supplies the authenticated operator identity when token protection is active.

POST /api/workbenches/{slug}/execution/authorize returns the decision and records it in the ledger. It does not execute the proposed command. The caller must use the decision before it releases the action. A direct worker tool invocation does not automatically pass through this route.

Sources: matching, conditions, decision route.

5. Release the backend loop process#

The named operation route supplies a concrete caller that obeys the broker decision. Operation routes default to disabled through REFALL_ENABLE_OPS. Named commands also require REFALL_ENABLE_OPS_COMMANDS. The command name must appear in REFALL_OPS_ALLOWED_COMMANDS. These switches enable functionality; they do not authenticate an operator.

Start requires stored, nonempty subject context. Its absence gives HTTP 409. When loop launch is enabled, Start and Update construct a run_local_command request for the standing loop. The request includes the subject path and a declared process effect. The backend records the authorization decision. Refusal gives HTTP 403 before the loop process starts.

Loop launch defaults to enabled once the operation route is enabled. Setting REFALL_ENABLE_LOOP_LAUNCH=false skips actual launch and its authorization check. Direct executor entry points and embedded launcher callbacks have their own calling paths. This launch gate describes the backend lifecycle route.

Source: backend lifecycle release.

6. Bound the assigned work#

The scheduler prioritizes pending actions, subject setup, fresh coverage, finding work, and later unit passes. Claims and per-target progress coordinate allocation. Eligible module selection checks dependencies, completed work, active target work, and module concurrency. Recorded paths allow applicable inclusion and exclusion checks.

Fresh characterization claims coverage directly. It uses the characterize task class and a 30-iteration conversation request. It does not use the later module eligibility branch. Later unit selection supplies the recorded path, but it does not supply unit_state. Module fields therefore have specific selection paths, as described in Work modules.

The dispatcher sends the workspace, objective, provider settings, and iteration limit to Agent Canvas. Global loop parallelism defaults to four work items. The runtime classifies recognized capability, scope, and operator-stop outcomes before retry. Those outcomes create decision obligations rather than ordinary automatic retries. Recoverable worker failures use the configured retry limit, which defaults to two attempts.

Context and scope also appear in the worker's objective. These instructions guide reasoning, target selection, resource use, and evidence submission. They do not turn an assignment path into a filesystem or network access restriction.

Sources: selection order, eligibility, dispatch, outcome classification.

7. Check continuation and preserve observations#

Resume preflight compares checkpoint input hashes with current source and configuration identities. A returned drift refusal stops the supported continuation path. The runtime retains a visible refusal event and decision state. This comparison requires prior checkpoints and the relevant API support. Missing optional support and some unavailable-service paths continue without a refusal.

During execution, polling reads available conversation events and workspace results. Completion handling first classifies the invocation, parses its output, and checks submission identity. It preserves available observations before handling the classified outcome or scheduling retry. Useful observations can therefore survive a failed conversation. A subject module without durable canonical observations remains unfinished.

Capture records what the worker supplied or what the runtime observed. It does not prove every recorded assertion or prevent the original tool action. Structured terminal submission is optional by default. Enable REFALL_REQUIRE_STRUCTURED_SUBMIT to require its contract during terminal validation.

Sources: resume comparison, resume caller, incremental ingestion.

8. Accept evidence and finding decisions separately#

Finding admission requires evidence, confidence, and source or artifact references. When an inventory is available, source anchors must belong to it. Without inventory, anchor membership produces a warning. External URL hosts require explicit inclusion in the scope overlay's external_targets. A candidate outside that declared scope is refused admission. The API records the refusal and creates review work.

This check acts on a proposed finding after worker activity. It does not intercept the network operation that might have produced the evidence. The scope overlay and a capability grant are separate records. Changing one does not automatically change the other.

Existing finding decisions use typed transitions. Direct validation updates cannot change finding status. False-positive, duplicate, downgrade, chain deferral, and live-validation decisions have distinct receipt requirements. Unresolved contradictory obligations can block suppressive transitions. Receipts with supplied hashes also receive source-root containment and current-content checks. An unhashed receipt does not activate those hash checks.

A refused transition preserves finding state and stores the refused attempt. A receipt establishes the required decision record and evidence references. It does not independently prove all factual claims or authenticate its declared author.

Sources: finding admission, typed transitions, hash checks.

9. Require resolution and review completion#

Pending actions preserve access requests, blocked scope, incomplete evidence, and decisions that still need attention. A required receipt type must match and include evidence references. Deferral and cancellation require receipt evidence. An untyped action completed as done does not universally require evidence.

Report assembly protects populated sections against structural downgrade. The default assembly path retains the current report and stores a diagnostic candidate when protected sections would disappear. An explicit allow_structural_downgrade argument bypasses that replacement guard. Generic object-content writes use a separate API path.

Closeout evaluates pending work, receipts, refused transitions, finding proof, expired claims, context, and report freshness. Blocking failures produce a blocked lifecycle result. Coverage below the default 95-percent threshold is advisory. Draft reports and current report objects can exist before closeout succeeds. The closeout gate does not control every object write, download, or external publication.

A closeout override requires identified checks and a nonempty receipt. An accepted override converts a matching failed check into a nonblocking warning. The ledger retains the exception and its stated reason. The override route records the supplied operator name without the capability-token authentication dependency. Deployment access control establishes who can reach that authority.

Sources: pending resolution, report protection, closeout, override route.

Worked example: an out-of-scope operation#

Assume the subject is alpha. Its write_subject grant permits /tmp/refall-subject. An agent proposes touch /etc/passwd with the target path /etc/passwd.

  1. Submit the action to the authorization route with its class, effects, command, and target.
  2. The broker compares the target with the grant's permitted path.
  3. The broker returns accepted: false and records the refusal.
  4. The calling executor keeps the action unreleased.
  5. The operator examines the requested target and the actual research need.
  6. Keep the refusal, or issue a separate grant for an approved operation.
  7. Submit a new authorization request after any approved change.

The authorization route itself never launches touch. Step 4 belongs to the caller that releases the operation. The backend standing-loop launch implements this release discipline directly. Worker tools need their own runtime enforcement or an integration that obeys broker decisions.

The existing broker tests cover path refusal, host refusal, method restrictions, expiry, and protected grant authentication.

An external validation request uses two additional campaign decisions. The operator can add an approved host to the scope overlay and grant the necessary network capability separately. A later finding can then cite that host under the admission rules. The runtime still needs an executor that obeys authorization and an environment with the intended network restrictions.

How this expresses the Ready Armor approach#

A useful control has a named authority, an explicit boundary, and an observable decision. REFALL applies that principle to campaign resources, brokered operations, assignments, evidence, and completion. Its controls make research progress and unfinished authority decisions reviewable across workers and sessions.

ARA and BRA describe related control principles through their own runtime and assessment architectures. REFALL implements its own scheduler, capability matcher, evidence records, and acceptance gates. It does not import their policy engines or supply their execution interception mechanisms. Read Research architecture for the wider system model.

REFALL AB work modules#

A work module declares a bounded research pass. The declaration identifies the work type, target source, prerequisites, selection rules, and additional objective. The scheduler evaluates modules against each target's current state.

Target sources#

Source valueTargetTypical use
subjectThe whole subject.Identification, background research, source-tool execution, or synthesis.
coverage_unitsA file, symbol, or line-range unit.Characterization, decomposition, review, or harness creation.
findingsA finding record.Reproduction, verification, or patch proposals.

A subject pass normally runs once for the subject. A later unit pass can run once for each eligible characterized unit. A finding pass can run once for each eligible finding. These selection paths use once_per_target and active-target tracking to prevent duplicate concurrent dispatch. Fresh characterization has a separate coverage-claim path.

Built-in packs#

PackModulesPurpose
baselinecharacterizeDescribe units with source anchors.
reverse_engineeringre_identify, re_decompose, re_reviewIdentify the subject, explain components, and review the decomposition.
security_assessmentsec_recon, sec_review, sec_verifyIdentify attack surfaces, examine candidate issues, and verify findings.
researchres_research, res_synthesisResearch the target class and compile the results.
developmentdev_harness, dev_patchDraft harnesses and propose fixes for findings.
dynamic_testingdyn_harness, dyn_verifyBuild an approved harness and record its runtime behavior.
static_analysissa_toolchain, sa_reviewProduce source-tool outputs and examine their meaning.

The default executable selection is security_assessment. Dependency resolution also adds its required characterization module. Select baseline explicitly for a characterization-only run. Packs can be combined. A pack is a convenience group rather than a global execution phase.

Dependencies and order#

The after list refers to modules completed on the same target. For example, re_review depends on re_decompose for that unit. It does not require decomposition of the whole repository.

The registry resolves missing built-in dependencies across packs. It rejects unknown dependencies and dependency cycles. Subject selection applies dependencies, completion tracking, active-target tracking, and module concurrency limits. Later unit selection also applies path rules to the recorded unit path. Finding selection applies path rules when a finding path is available. Lower numerical priority runs first within the relevant selection.

Fresh breadth uses coverage claims rather than the module eligibility function. The loop attaches the first active breadth module and always dispatches the characterize task class. That task receives the module objective and a limit of 30 iterations. The global loop concurrency limit controls these tasks. Breadth selection does not apply module path filters or per-module concurrency limits. Use dependency-free coverage modules for characterization. Use modules with an after dependency for filtered later passes.

The standing loop adds a broader dispatch order:

  1. Claim pending actions and requested threat-model work.
  2. Select eligible subject modules.
  3. Claim fresh coverage units for breadth.
  4. Select finding-specific modules.
  5. Select later passes on characterized units.

Fresh breadth takes precedence over repeated deep work on an initial subset. Finding verification and later unit work continue after fresh units are exhausted.

Configure a subject#

Store the configuration in the workbench refall_modules custom field. The loader accepts an object or a JSON string. The workbench metadata API represents custom field values as strings. Use JSON text when updating this field through that API.

A combined source-research configuration is:

json
{
  "packs": [
    "reverse_engineering",
    "security_assessment",
    "static_analysis"
  ],
  "overrides": {
    "sec_review": {
      "path_globs": ["src/**", "lib/**"],
      "exclude_globs": ["**/generated/**"],
      "max_parallel": 2
    }
  }
}

This selects subject identification, decomposition, review, source analysis, security review, and finding verification. It limits the security review pass to selected paths and two concurrent tasks.

A custom subject pass can be added as follows:

json
{
  "packs": ["baseline", "reverse_engineering"],
  "modules": [
    {
      "id": "interface_catalog",
      "task_class": "research",
      "source": "subject",
      "priority": 25,
      "max_parallel": 1,
      "objective": "Catalog documented interfaces and anchor each entry to the subject material."
    }
  ]
}

The custom objective becomes part of a bounded task. The module uses the normal context, evidence, persistence, and result-processing path. Its task class must exist in the router. A declaration does not install a new tool or execution service.

Select targets and limits#

FieldMeaning
idStable module identifier.
task_classRouter task class.
sourceSubject, coverage units, or findings.
afterPrerequisites on the same target.
unit_stateState predicate for eligibility callers that supply the target state.
path_globsIncluded paths for later unit passes and findings with a recorded path.
exclude_globsExcluded paths for those same selection paths.
priorityNumerical ordering value.
max_parallelModule concurrency limit for subject, finding, and later unit selection.
objectiveAdditional specialist instructions.
enabledWhether the module participates.
once_per_targetWhether completed targets remain excluded.
packModule group label.

The later unit scheduler draws targets from its characterized-unit collection. It does not supply unit_state to the eligibility function. Its target collection and module dependencies establish that path's progress requirements.

The disabled list can disable selected module identifiers. The overrides map can adjust a built-in declaration. Review dependencies when disabling prerequisite modules.

Adapt the research objective#

For architecture mapping, select baseline and reverse-engineering modules. Use facts, leads, flows, and saved diagrams as the principal outputs. The refall_no_findings field selects the available mapping-oriented output contract and report behavior.

For a security campaign, combine security assessment with research or static analysis when useful. For remediation work, add development modules and supply the required write authority. For runtime examination, supply a subject harness and the necessary capability grants.

Preserve prior work#

The scheduler stores progress in .refall/module_progress.json. It records completed module identifiers, characterized units, and known findings. Later unit objectives tell workers to read prior determinations, findings, shared notes, and saved analysis artifacts. A successful later pass extends the evidence without submitting the characterization result again.

Subject modules must produce durable facts, leads, findings, or flows. A pass without canonical output creates an ingestion-review action and remains unfinished. This requirement keeps a completed task from becoming an empty progress marker.

Sources: WorkModule, registry, scheduler, dispatch order.

REFALL AB architecture map#

REFALL AB connects an operator workbench, backend control services, a persistent research loop, specialist execution, and analysis resources. The subject workbench is the common state boundary. Read Research architecture for the design rationale. Read the Technical codex for the implementation path.

The backend implementation retains the ArcticBase name in paths and process names. The product name is REFALL AB.

Service flow#

State ownership#

Workbench metadata and objects#

The backend stores the subject identity, source path, display theme, custom module settings, and report pointer. Objects hold context, HTML reports, uploaded material, and published artifacts. refall_current_report_object_id identifies the current report explicitly.

Coverage storage#

refall_coverage.db stores coverage units, evidence anchors, finding state, transition receipts, pending actions, capabilities, and supporting research records. A coverage unit includes ownership, lease expiry, summary, sensitivity, touched data, flows, and leads. Coverage percentages summarize recorded unit state.

Evidence ledger#

refall_ledger.jsonl stores facts, leads, findings, validation, artifacts, and important decisions. Entries identify the workbench and relevant task or lane. This ledger is distinct from the runtime database and agent conversation archive.

Subject runtime#

.refall/runtime/state.sqlite stores events, sessions, observations, retry state, artifacts, manifests, and checkpoints. .refall/runtime/artifacts/ holds artifact content. Runtime projections expose observations, evidence relationships, and nonfatal errors through workbench APIs.

Scheduling state#

.refall/loop_state.json preserves active conversations and iteration state. .refall/module_progress.json preserves completed passes and known targets. .refall/blackboard.json provides compact shared notes. These records support continuation without making a conversation transcript the research database.

Research work and provider roles#

The manager examines context, resources, unresolved work, and current proof. The standing loop turns that state into bounded assignments. Claude and Codex use configured ACP lanes through Agent Canvas. The optional Grok role is controlled by the host manager in a separate sandbox.

The module registry can combine source understanding, security review, research, development, static analysis, and dynamic examination. Each module has a target source and optional local dependencies. The scheduler prioritizes pending actions, subject setup, fresh breadth, finding work, and later unit passes.

Control points#

Source projection prepares the configured container location and reports existing mount permissions. Inventory records content identity rather than preventing file access. The capability broker evaluates presented action requests against grants. Backend Start and Update enforce a refusal before loop process release. The generic authorization route returns a decision without executing the command.

Grant and revoke authentication requires REFALL_CAPABILITY_OPERATOR_TOKEN_PATH. The unset default retains caller-supplied grantor identities. Task context supplies scope guidance; Agent Canvas and deployment permissions supply the execution boundary. The promotion gate checks candidate evidence, source identity, and external scope. The disposition gate checks finding transitions and typed receipts. The closeout gate checks the persistent campaign state and report freshness.

These control points govern different transitions. A successful process launch does not establish a valid finding. A valid finding does not establish that the campaign is complete. Draft report objects can exist before the closeout gate passes. Read Control in depth for action gates, record gates, guidance, observations, and explicit exceptions.

Recovery and publication#

HTTP retries handle transient service failures. Terminal handling classifies the invocation and preserves output before handling failure or scheduling retry. Checkpoints and manifests connect resumed work to source and configuration identities. The watchdog and supervisor expose stalled or degraded execution and bounded recovery.

Draft and enrichment stages compile stored evidence. A replacement guard protects populated architecture, methods, and flow sections. Closeout then reports blocking obligations and advisory warnings separately.

REFALL AB installation#

Requirements#

Use Python 3.12 or later for the backend. Use uv to install the backend dependencies. The frontend uses pnpm and Node.js. The Docker build uses Node.js 24 and Python 3.13.

Research execution requires an Agent Canvas/OpenHands service with its Automation API. A manager also requires the selected provider CLI. Docker is necessary for container deployment and Codebadger.

Install the backend#

Run these commands from the refall directory.

  1. Install the backend and development dependencies.
bash
   uv sync --project arcticbase/backend --group dev
  1. Install the executor dependencies in the same environment.
bash
   uv pip install --python arcticbase/backend/.venv/bin/python -r coverage_service/requirements.txt
  1. Select the repository directory.
bash
   export REFALL_REPO_ROOT="$PWD"
   export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/arcticbase/backend/src"
   export PATH="$PWD/arcticbase/backend/.venv/bin:$PATH"

Build the web interface#

  1. Install the frontend dependencies.
bash
   pnpm --dir arcticbase/frontend install --frozen-lockfile
  1. Build the web interface.
bash
   pnpm --dir arcticbase/frontend build

Configure local services#

  1. Select the local service address.
bash
   export ARCTIC_BASE_HOST=127.0.0.1
   export ARCTIC_BASE_PORT=7673
   export REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7673
   export REFALL_WORKBENCH_BASE="$REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL"
  1. Select writable storage paths.
bash
   export ARCTIC_BASE_DATA="$PWD/data/arcticbase"
   export REFALL_DATA_ROOT="$PWD/data/refall"
   export REFALL_SUBJECT_ROOT="$REFALL_DATA_ROOT/subjects"
   export ARCTIC_BASE_FRONTEND_DIST="$PWD/arcticbase/frontend/dist"
   export ARCTIC_BASE_SEED_DATA="$PWD/arcticbase/backend/seed"
  1. Set the Agent Canvas address and API key path.
bash
   export REFALL_OPENHANDS_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8000
   export REFALL_OPENHANDS_API_KEY_PATH="$HOME/.openhands/agent-canvas/api-key.txt"
  1. Enable the operation routes.
bash
   export REFALL_ENABLE_OPS=true
   export REFALL_ENABLE_OPS_COMMANDS=true
  1. Start the backend.
bash
   python -m arctic_base
  1. Open http://127.0.0.1:7673.
  1. Read the health response.
bash
   curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:7673/api/health

The default backend address uses a detected LAN address when no host override is set. The explicit local address above keeps all local examples consistent. For remote access, set the public URL and listen address for that deployment.

Configure execution#

  1. Install and configure Agent Canvas/OpenHands separately.
  2. Mount the repository and subject directories in the agent container.
  3. Set REFALL_WORKSPACE to the container repository path.
  4. Set REFALL_SUBJECT_WORKSPACE_ROOT to the container subject parent.
  5. Configure the selected provider CLI.
  6. Run the subject diagnosis procedure before the first research loop.

The default container repository path is /projects/REFALL-V10. The default container subject parent is /projects. The host source path and container source path must refer to the same subject files.

Operator authentication and action release#

Set REFALL_CAPABILITY_OPERATOR_TOKEN_PATH to a host-managed token file to authenticate capability grant and revoke requests. Keep this file outside worker access. Send its value in X-REFALL-Operator-Token from the authenticated operator client. The backend uses constant-time comparison and records the authenticated grantor as operator. An unavailable token file gives HTTP 503; an invalid token gives HTTP 403.

The default unset value disables token authentication on these routes. Grantor fields then come from the request body. The browser capability client does not attach this token automatically. Use a host-side authenticated client to establish grants in a protected deployment. Operation enable switches control functionality rather than caller identity. The closeout override route records the supplied operator name and has no capability-token authentication dependency. Restrict API reachability to the intended callers.

The authorization endpoint returns a decision without executing commands. Backend Start and Update obey that decision before process launch. Worker tools need their actual runtime permissions or an executor integration that obeys the broker. Read Control in depth for applicable scope fields, defaults, and record gates.

REFALL AB operating procedures#

Use these procedures from the repository directory. Complete Installation first. The CLI uses REFALL_WORKBENCH_BASE or REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL to select the workbench service.

Create a subject#

A subject is the source tree, binary, or system under examination. A workbench stores the subject context, research records, and reports. Use one workbench for each subject.

  1. Create the subject workbench.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor subject create example --source-path /absolute/path/to/example
  1. Generate the shared context.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor ops command context example
  1. Examine the stored context in the workbench.
  2. Examine the source inventory and scope.
  3. Run the diagnosis command.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor ops command doctor example
  1. Get the workload estimate.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor ops command estimate example

Grant a launch capability#

A capability is an operator grant for a specified action and scope. A loop launch requires a subject-scoped run_local_command grant when launch execution is enabled. The operator token comes from REFALL_CAPABILITY_OPERATOR_TOKEN_PATH when that setting is configured.

  1. Submit the launch grant through the workbench capability interface.
  2. Select run_local_command as the action class.
  3. Set the scope to the subject source path.
  4. Record the reason for the grant.

The capability endpoint is /api/workbenches/{slug}/capabilities/grant. Agents cannot grant themselves permission for live actions.

Run research#

Stored context is necessary before the first loop launch.

  1. Start the loop.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor loop start example
  1. Examine the operation status.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor ops status
  1. Examine coverage, ledger records, findings, and pending actions in the workbench.
  2. Resolve open capability requests and scope decisions.
  3. Run a bounded update when necessary.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor loop update example

Start Loop and Update in the web interface use the same operation routes. Doctor examines services, paths, capabilities, provider commands, and supporting tools. Estimate measures the work represented by the current subject inventory.

Prepare a report#

  1. Create the report draft.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor report draft example
  1. Enrich the report.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor report enrich example
  1. Examine the current report in the workbench.
  2. Examine the closeout gate.
bash
   curl -fsS "$REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/api/workbenches/example/closeout/gate"
  1. Resolve each open condition.
  2. Request closeout.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor loop closeout example

Report enrichment adds evidence context, related findings, remediation information, and visual evidence. The closeout gate identifies pending actions, refused transitions, incomplete validation, stale reports, and missing receipts.

Examine the ledger#

The ledger is a sequence of evidence and decision records. Each significant research result, disposition, capability decision, and report change belongs in the ledger.

bash
curl -fsS "$REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/api/workbenches/example/ledger/entries"

Stop local services#

  1. Examine the shutdown actions.
bash
   python3 refall_down.py --dry-run --include-serena
  1. Stop the local runtime.
bash
   python3 refall_down.py --include-serena

REFALL Manager Operating Guide#

The manager operates REFALL AB and coordinates specialist research. ArcticBase is the backend implementation name. Use REFALL AB as the product name in status messages and procedures.

Read first#

  1. Read starthere/ in numeric order.
  2. Read AGENTS.md.
  3. Read docs/manager/AGENTS.md.
  4. Read CODEX.md or CLAUDE.md for the selected role.
  5. Read the subject context before you claim work.

The alternate startup pack is docs/codex-startup/*.md. Read Operating procedures for the command sequence.

Prepare infrastructure#

Run these commands from the repository directory.

bash
export REFALL_REPO_ROOT="$PWD"
export REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7673
export REFALL_WORKBENCH_BASE="$REFALL_PUBLIC_BASE_URL"
export REFALL_OPENHANDS_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8000
  1. Complete the installation procedure.
  2. Read /api/health.
  3. Read /api/refall/ops/status.
  4. Examine /api/refall/ops/infra and /api/refall/ops/agents.
  5. Examine Agent Canvas/OpenHands connectivity.
  6. Examine the selected provider CLI and subject mounts.
  7. Examine remote resource access when the subject requires it.

Operation routes require REFALL_ENABLE_OPS=true. Named commands require REFALL_ENABLE_OPS_COMMANDS=true. The allowlist must include the requested command.

Create the subject#

  1. Create the workbench.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor subject create example --source-path /absolute/path/to/example
  1. Examine the source path from the backend host.
  2. Examine the matching source mount from the agent container.
  3. Set the subject scope and exclusions.

Create Workbench Theme#

Use PUT /api/workbenches/{slug}/theme to set the workbench appearance. The JSON body contains the complete theme document in raw. The theme document contains YAML frontmatter and Markdown. Read /api/agent/conventions for the required tokens and layout values.

Generate Context#

  1. Request context generation.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor ops command context example
  1. Read /api/workbenches/example/coverage/context.
  2. Examine the stored context.md content in info_md.
  3. Examine source inventory, scope overlay, and the threat model.
  4. Run doctor example and estimate example when readiness is uncertain.

A loop cannot start without stored context. The manager uses the context to constrain discovery, validation, and report preparation.

Start Loop#

  1. Obtain a subject-scoped run_local_command capability from the operator.
  2. Start the loop.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor loop start example
  1. Examine the operation response and agent state.

With REFALL_ENABLE_LOOP_LAUNCH=true, start launches ref_all_executor.standing_loop with --max-cycles 0. Update launches the same runner with --max-cycles 1. The manager must not replace this runner with undocumented work in chat.

Monitor and recover#

Examine these records during each manager cycle:

  • Coverage statistics, claim leases, and the coverage gate.
  • Source inventory and scope overlay.
  • Pending actions and capability requests.
  • Runtime manifest, observations, artifacts, and the evidence graph.
  • Current findings, disposition refusals, and report freshness.

The live diagnosis route is /api/refall/ops/debug/{subject}/live. The run manifest is /api/workbenches/{slug}/runtime/manifest. Local loop state uses .refall/loop_state.json. The nonfatal error route is a read-only projection.

  1. Resolve pending actions before ordinary coverage work.
  2. Examine failures before you request another cycle.
  3. Request a bounded update when recovery is appropriate.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor loop update example
  1. Append important decisions and observations to the ledger.

The watchdog and supervisor preserve liveness information. The recovery policy restores failed services. It does not use service failure as a reason to tear down the stack. Review stale loop state before you start replacement work.

Specialist output#

Specialists return fenced refall-submit JSON with schema refall.submit.v1. Use the task_result_submit event and a stable submission_id. Evidence-bearing results require evidence, confidence, limitations, and source anchors or artifact references. Use REFALL_REQUIRE_STRUCTURED_SUBMIT=true to require valid structured output.

The executor ignores duplicate structured submissions. It stores a nested finding before it applies proposed transitions. New findings begin as PROVISIONALLY_VALID or NEEDS_RESEARCH. VALID describes finding status. LIVE_CONFIRMED describes evidence quality. Keep these properties separate.

Submit suppressive changes through /api/workbenches/{slug}/findings/{finding_id}/transitions. Use typed evidence receipts. Include source_hashes when proof depends on exact source or configuration bytes. A stale receipt is refused.

A scope_blocked result creates a scope decision. A capability_missing result creates a capability request. Neither result completes the unit. The specialist cannot authorize its own live action.

Remote SSH Resources#

REFALL_SSH_RESOURCE_ALIASES selects remote resources from the configured allowlist. The current allowlist is sectortw,sectortl. Set an empty value to disable remote resources.

  1. Assign a remote resource only when the task requires it.
  2. Run the command with ssh <alias> <command>.
  3. Record the alias, command, evidence, and limitations in the submission.

Grok is not an SSH resource. Its optional worker is host-orchestrated inside a sandbox. It must not receive host credentials. The manager transfers permitted subject material into the sandbox and records its results through REFALL APIs.

Analysis and visual evidence#

Run source analysis with toolchain/run.sh when it supplies useful evidence. Start Codebadger for property graphs, data flow, taint analysis, or slicing when necessary. Preserve the command and input identity with analysis artifacts. Link screenshots, graphs, CodeCharta views, and other visual evidence to the supported finding.

Closeout#

  1. Resolve pending actions and refused transitions.
  2. Complete the required validation.
  3. Create the report draft.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor report draft example
  1. Enrich the report.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor report enrich example
  1. Read /api/workbenches/example/closeout/gate.
  2. Resolve each condition or record an operator override receipt.
  3. Request closeout.
bash
   python3 -m ref_all_executor loop closeout example

Read Evidence requirements and API reference for the complete contracts.

REFALL AB API reference#

The backend exposes an HTTP API. Use the configured service URL as the base for each route. Get the running schema from /openapi.json. Read interactive API documentation at /docs.

Subjects and operations#

Named commands include context, coverage, threat-model, doctor, estimate, start, update, and closeout. Operation commands require the corresponding enable settings. Enabled process launches through Start and Update also require a scoped capability grant. A refused authorization returns HTTP 403 before process release.

The following paths are relative to /api/workbenches/{slug}. Replace {slug} with the subject workbench identifier.

Use the running schema for request bodies and supported methods. The coverage API includes claims, research units, findings, investigations, and statistics.

Capability and operator boundaries#

POST /api/workbenches/{slug}/execution/authorize returns and records an authorization decision. It does not execute the requested command. Callers must obey the decision before action release.

Capability grant and revoke authentication activates with REFALL_CAPABILITY_OPERATOR_TOKEN_PATH. Protected requests supply X-REFALL-Operator-Token. The unset default accepts caller-supplied identity fields without token authentication. The closeout override route separately records a supplied operator name, check IDs, reason, and receipt. It does not use the capability-token dependency. Read Control in depth for route responsibilities and deployment authority.

Finding transitions#

Submit a transition with POST /api/workbenches/{slug}/findings/{finding_id}/transitions. Read transition history with GET on the same route. Read refused transitions at /api/workbenches/{slug}/disposition/refusals.

A transition identifies the current state, proposed state, reason, receipt type, and supporting evidence. Source hashes can bind the receipt to exact source bytes. Read Evidence for the status and receipt models.

Workbench presentation#

Use PUT /api/workbenches/{slug}/theme to replace the workbench theme. The request body contains a raw field with YAML frontmatter and Markdown. Read /api/agent/conventions for the theme format.

Reports#

REFALL report routes use /api/refall/reports/. The report module serves the specification and report assembly functions. The pinned workbench report route selects the current report explicitly.

Ledger and wishlist procedures#

Use POST /api/workbenches/{slug}/ledger/entries to append a supported entry kind. Use GET on the same route to list records. List filters are kind, lane, severity, and since. The ledger exposes lookup and statistics routes without entry update or delete operations.

Use POST and GET on /api/workbenches/{slug}/coverage/wishlist to record and list wishlist rows. List requests can select status. Delivery records use provided; the watchdog appends that row separately from the original open request. The compatibility coverage service has its own /wishlist and /wishlist_resolve routes. Read Ledger and wishlist for payloads and the distinction between the route families.

FIELD GUIDE / 173 MIN READ

REFALL AB evidence requirements#

Evidence model#

An observation records what the specialist examined or measured. A lead records a question that requires more work. A finding records a supported security conclusion. A receipt records evidence for a decision or state transition.

Each finding includes the affected component, source anchors, reproduction procedure, impact, likelihood, remediation, and verification state. Evidence-bearing submissions also include confidence and limitations. Use artifact references when source anchors cannot represent the proof.

Structured submissions#

Return terminal results in a fenced refall-submit JSON block. The schema name is refall.submit.v1. The submission event is task_result_submit. Use submission_id to identify the result.

The executor validates the payload before it applies coverage updates. Duplicate structured submissions do not create duplicate findings. ref_all_executor/contract_payloads.py supplies payload helpers. Backend DTO validation is in arcticbase/backend/src/arctic_base/refall/contracts.py.

Set REFALL_REQUIRE_STRUCTURED_SUBMIT=true to require valid structured results. A missing or malformed result then creates pending work instead of completed coverage. Legacy terminal markers remain a compatibility format.

Finding status and evidence quality#

Status and evidence quality describe different properties. Status describes the research workflow. Quality describes the strength of the proof.

StatusMeaning
PROVISIONALLY_VALIDCandidate finding that requires review.
NEEDS_RESEARCHFinding that requires more examination.
VALIDFinding that passed the required checks.
FALSE_POSITIVERejected finding with a supporting receipt.
DUPLICATEFinding equivalent to a canonical finding.
CHAINABLE_DEFERREDPreserved primitive that requires chain analysis.

Evidence quality uses HYPOTHESIS, CODE_CONFIRMED, and LIVE_CONFIRMED. Static confirmation does not establish runtime exploitability.

Disposition receipts#

Submit status changes through the finding transition endpoint. Use typed evidence receipts for rejection, duplicates, deferral, severity reduction, and quality reduction.

Receipt typeEvidence
code_anchorSource or binary location that supports the claim.
live_reproReproduced runtime behavior.
non_reachability_proofRouting or configuration proof that excludes the sink.
duplicate_equivalenceSame root cause, sink, and remediation as the canonical finding.
scope_boundaryRecorded scope or exclusion boundary.
downgrade_with_trigger_inventoryRelevant trigger paths and reason for reduced severity.
chain_preservationPreserved primitive and remaining chain questions.
patch_verificationPatch evidence and verification results.
operator_overrideExplicit operator decision and reason.

A duplicate receipt identifies duplicate_of. Receipts can include source_hashes. The backend refuses a receipt when its source or configuration hashes are stale. Accepted and refused transitions remain in the ledger.

Pending actions and capabilities#

Pending actions preserve unfinished obligations. Examples include missing validation, exhausted retries, scope decisions, and operator requests. A direct capability_missing result creates a capability request. A direct scope_blocked result creates a scope_decision action. Neither result completes the research unit.

Capabilities restrict live actions to the operator-approved class and scope. The worker cannot approve its own live actions.

Closeout and reports#

The closeout gate checks unresolved pending actions, refused transitions, suppressive finding changes, report freshness, and validation proof. Resolve each condition or record an operator override receipt.

Reports include scope, methods, findings, evidence, limitations, remediation, and verification state. A visual evidence pack can contain screenshots, traces, CodeCharta views, Codebadger output, or exploit-flow diagrams. Link each visual to the claim that it supports.

The ledger can record codebadger-toolchain-not-run when that tool did not run. The publication flow records vendor-cna-report-generated for the corresponding report artifact. Read the runtime report specification in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-refall-report-format-spec.md.

scip/SCIP indexes.
logs/Per-tool output.
run_manifest.jsonStep results and return codes.

Manage optional services#

bash
toolchain/ctl.sh status
toolchain/ctl.sh up serena
toolchain/ctl.sh down serena
toolchain/ctl.sh up codebadger-mcp
toolchain/ctl.sh restart python-lsp-server
toolchain/ctl.sh down

ctl.sh up preserves an already healthy service. ctl.sh down first sends TERM to the service process group. It sends KILL if the process does not exit. The registry is config/services.json. Only entries in services[] are active.

Codebadger#

Start Codebadger when the subject needs property graphs, taint analysis, or slicing. The installer or first start obtains the pinned Codebadger source. Docker supplies its supporting services.

Place local source under toolchain/third_party/codebadger/playground/subjects/<subject>. Use /app/playground/subjects/<subject> as the corresponding container path. The MCP service binds to loopback on port 4242. Its configuration is available through toolchain/bin/codebadger-service mcp-config.

Agent configuration#

MCP configuration examples are in config/. Use serena-mcp-config.json, codebase-memory-mcp-config.json, or codebadger-mcp-config.json for the required service. The service registry also contains disabled extension slots. Copy a slot into services[] only after its command and health check are configured.
